title.zh: 卷一百七十二 列傳第一百二十二: 令狐楚 牛僧孺 蕭俛 李石
title.en: Volume 172 Biographies 122: Ling Huchu, Niu Sengru, Xiaomian, Li Shi
title.raw: 卷一百七十二 列傳第一百二十二: 令狐楚 牛僧孺 蕭俛 李石 Volume 172 Biographies 122: Ling Huchu, Niu Sengru, Xiaomian, Li Shi

sentences.zh: 李宗閔，字損之，宗室鄭王元懿之後。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin, courtesy name Sunzhi, was a descendant of the imperial clansman Prince Yuan of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin, whose courtesy name was Sunzhi, was a descendant of Prince Yuan of Zheng of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 祖自仙，楚州別駕。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zixian was Vice-Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zixian had served as vice-prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父，宗正卿，出為華州刺史、鎮國軍潼關防禦等使。

translations.literal: His father, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, went out to serve as Governor of Huazhou and Commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and Tong Pass Defense, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: His father, who had been director of the imperial clan court, later went out to serve as governor of Huazhou and commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and Tong Pass defense, among other posts.

sentences.zh: 兄夷簡，元和中宰相。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yijian was a chief minister in the Yuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yijian had been chief minister during the Yuanhe reign.

sentences.zh: 宗閔，貞元二十一年進士擢第，元和四年，復登制舉賢良方正科。

translations.literal: Zongmin passed the jinshi examination in Zhenyuan year twenty-one, and in Yuanhe year four again passed the imperial examination for Worthy, Good, Upright, and Correct men.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin passed the jinshi examination in Zhenyuan year twenty-one, and in Yuanhe year four again passed the imperial examination for Worthy, Good, Upright, and Correct men.

sentences.zh: 初，宗閔與牛僧孺同年登進士第，又與僧孺同年登制科。

translations.literal: At first Zongmin and Niu Sengru passed the jinshi examination in the same year, and Sengru also passed the decree examination in the same year as he.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zongmin and Niu Sengru had passed the jinshi examination in the same year, and Zongmin had also passed the special decree examination in the same year as Sengru.

sentences.zh: 應制之歲，李吉甫為宰相當國，宗閔、僧孺對策，指切時政之失，言甚鯁直，無所回避。

translations.literal: In the year they answered the decree examination, Li Jifu was chief minister holding power; Zongmin and Sengru submitted their policy essays, pointing to faults in current government, speaking very bluntly without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of that examination, Li Jifu was chief minister and held the reins of government. Zongmin and Sengru submitted their policy essays, criticizing the failings of current policy in language so blunt that they held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 考策官楊於陵、韋貫之、李益等又第其策為中等，又為不中第者註解牛、李策語，同為唱誹。

translations.literal: The examiners Yang Yuling, Wei Guanzhi, Li Yi, and others also ranked their essays in the middle grade, and again annotated the policy language of Niu and Li for those who had not passed, all joining in ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners Yang Yuling, Wei Guanzhi, Li Yi, and others nevertheless ranked their essays in the middle tier, and they also annotated the policy language of Niu and Li for those who had failed the examination, joining together in mockery.

sentences.zh: 又言翰林學士王涯甥皇甫湜中選，考核之際，不先上言。

translations.literal: They also said that Hanlin Academician Wang Ya's nephew Huangfu Shi had been selected, and that at the time of evaluation they had not reported this to the throne first.
translations.idiomatic: They also charged that Wang Ya's nephew Huangfu Shi, a Hanlin academician's kin, had been chosen in the selection, and that the examiners had failed to report this to the throne beforehand during the evaluation.

sentences.zh: 裴垍時為學士，居中覆視，無所異同。

translations.literal: Pei Ji was then an academician and reviewed the matter from within; he found nothing different.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji was then a Hanlin academician and reviewed the matter from within the palace; he found no discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 吉甫泣訴於上前，憲宗不獲已，罷王涯、裴垍學士。

translations.literal: Jifu wept and complained before the emperor; Emperor Xianzong, having no choice, dismissed Wang Ya and Pei Ji as academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu wept and lodged his complaint before the emperor. Unable to refuse him, Emperor Xianzong dismissed Wang Ya and Pei Ji from their Hanlin posts.

sentences.zh: 垍守戶部侍郎，涯守都官員外郎，吏部尚書楊於陵出為嶺南節度使，吏部員外郎韋貫之出為果州刺史。

translations.literal: Pei Ji remained Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, and Wang Ya remained Vice Director of the Bureau of Justice. Yang Yuling, Minister of Personnel, was sent out as military governor of Lingnan, and Wei Guanzhi, Vice Director of Personnel, as prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji remained Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, and Wang Ya remained Vice Director of the Bureau of Justice. Yang Yuling, Minister of Personnel, was sent out as military governor of Lingnan, and Wei Guanzhi, Vice Director of Personnel, as prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 王涯再貶虢州司馬，貫之再貶巴州刺史；

translations.literal: Wang Ya was demoted again to Defender of Guozhou, and Guanzhi was demoted again to Prefect of Bazhou;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya was demoted again to defender of Guozhou, and Guanzhi again to prefect of Bazhou;

sentences.zh: 僧孺、宗閔亦久之不調，隨牒諸侯府。

translations.literal: Sengru and Zongmin also went long without reassignment and followed appointment documents to the offices of regional lords.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru and Zongmin likewise went for a long time without regular appointments and took up posts in the secretariats of various regional lords.

sentences.zh: 七年，吉甫卒，方入朝為監察御史，累遷禮部員外郎，

translations.literal: In the seventh year Jifu died; only then did he enter court as Supervising Censor and was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Jifu died, and only then did Zongmin enter court service as supervising censor, rising in succession to vice director in the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年，宰相裴度出征吳元濟，奏宗閔為彰義軍觀察判官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, Chief Minister Pei Du campaigned against Wu Yuanji and memorialized that Zongmin be made Administrative Aide to the Zhangyi Army observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, When chief minister Pei Du marched against Wu Yuanji, he recommended Zongmin as administrative aide to the Zhangyi Army observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊平，遷駕部郎中，又以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was transferred to Director in the Bureau of the Imperial Stud and also served in his original office as drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed he was promoted to director in the bureau of the imperial stud and also continued in that office as drafter of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, he was appointed Attendant Drafting at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Zongmin was appointed attendant drafting at the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時自宗正卿出刺華州，父子同時承恩制，人士榮之，

translations.literal: At that time his father had gone out from the Directorate of the Imperial Clan to govern Huazhou; father and son at the same time received imperial favor in edicts, and gentlemen honored them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his father had left the directorate of the imperial clan to govern Huazhou, and father and son alike received edicts of imperial favor at the same time—a distinction that men of standing greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，子婿蘇巢於錢徽下進士及第，其年，巢覆落。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, His son-in-law Su Chao passed the jinshi examination under Qian Hui; that year Chao was struck from the rolls upon review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing, His son-in-law Su Chao had passed the jinshi examination under examiner Qian Hui, but that same year Chao's degree was revoked upon reexamination.

sentences.zh: 宗閔涉請托，貶劍州刺史。

translations.literal: Zongmin was implicated in solicitation and was demoted to Prefect of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin was implicated in improper solicitation and demoted to prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時李吉甫子德裕為翰林學士，錢徽榜出，德裕與同職李紳、元稹連衡言於上前，雲徽受請托，所試不公，故致重覆。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jifu's son Deyu was a Hanlin Academician; when Qian Hui's examination list was issued, Deyu together with his colleagues Li Shen and Yuan Zhen joined in speaking before the emperor, saying Hui had accepted solicitation, that the examination was unjust, and that this had caused the reexamination.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jifu's son Deyu was a Hanlin academician. When Qian Hui's examination results were published, Deyu joined his colleagues Li Shen and Yuan Zhen in telling the emperor that Hui had accepted improper solicitations, that the examination had been unfair, and that this was why the results had to be reviewed again.

sentences.zh: 比相嫌惡，因是列為朋黨，皆挾邪取權，兩相傾軋。

translations.literal: They came to hate one another; on this account they were classed as factional partisans, all grasping evil to seize power, the two sides overthrowing each other.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides came to detest each other and were accordingly branded as rival factions, each group using unscrupulous means to seize power and the two camps striving to crush one another.

sentences.zh: 自是紛紜排陷，垂四十年。

translations.literal: From this time forward there were unceasing accusations and entrapments, lasting nearly forty years.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on there was an unending stream of accusations and political entrapments that lasted for nearly forty years.

sentences.zh: 復入為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He again entered court as Attendant Drafting at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as attendant drafting at the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，權知禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he was appointed acting Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he was appointed acting vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 四年，貢舉事畢，權知兵部侍郎，

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the tribute examination was finished, he was appointed acting Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after the civil examinations were concluded, he was appointed acting vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 寶曆元年，正拜兵部侍郎，父憂免。

translations.literal: In Baoli year one, he was formally appointed Vice Minister of War but then left office to observe mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoli year one, he was formally appointed Vice Minister of War but then left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，起為吏部侍郎，賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: In Taihe year two, he was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of Personnel and was granted the gold-and-purple ceremonial robe.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year two, he was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of Personnel and was granted the gold-and-purple ceremonial robe.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year he was made associate chief minister while retaining his existing office.

sentences.zh: 時裴度薦李德裕，將大用。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Du recommended Li Deyu, intending to employ him in a major capacity.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Du had recommended Li Deyu and intended to give him major responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 德裕自浙西入朝，為中人助宗閔者所沮，復出鎮。

translations.literal: Deyu came to court from Zhexi but was obstructed by eunuchs who aided Zongmin, and again went out to command a defense command.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu came to court from Zhexi but was blocked by eunuchs who supported Zongmin, and was sent out again to command a military region.

sentences.zh: 尋引牛僧孺同知政事，二人唱和，凡德裕之黨皆逐之。

translations.literal: Soon he brought in Niu Sengru to share in governing affairs; the two acted in concert, and all of Deyu's partisans were driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he brought Niu Sengru in to share governing authority. Acting in concert, the two drove out every partisan of Deyu.

sentences.zh: 累轉中書侍郎、集賢大學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Jixian Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to vice director of the secretariat and grand academician of the Jixian Institute.

sentences.zh: 七年，德裕作相。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Deyu became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Deyu became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 六月，罷宗閔知政事，檢校禮部尚書、同平章事、興元尹、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Zongmin was removed from governing affairs and made Honorary Minister of Rites, Associate Chief Minister, Administrator of Xingyuan, and Military Governor of the Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zongmin was removed from governing affairs and appointed honorary minister of rites, associate chief minister, administrator of Xingyuan, and military governor of the Shannan West circuit.

sentences.zh: 宗閔為吏部侍郎時，因駙馬都尉沈結托女學士宋若憲及知樞密楊承和，二人數稱之於上前，故獲徵用。

translations.literal: When Zongmin was Vice Minister of Personnel, through the Princess's Consort Commandant Shen he entrusted the female academician Song Ruoxian and the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yang Chenghe; the two repeatedly praised him before the emperor, and so he obtained appointment.
translations.idiomatic: While Zongmin was vice minister of personnel, he had relied on the princess's consort commandant Shen to entreat the female academician Song Ruoxian and the commissioner of military affairs Yang Chenghe; the two repeatedly praised him before the emperor, and on that account he had won appointment.

sentences.zh: 及德裕秉政，群邪不悅，而鄭註、李訓深惡之。

translations.literal: When Deyu held power, the wicked were displeased, and Zheng Zhu and Li Xun deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu held power, the corrupt were displeased, and Zheng Zhu and Li Xun hated him intensely.

sentences.zh: 文宗乃復召宗閔於興元，為中書侍郎、平章事，命德裕代宗閔為興元尹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong then recalled Zongmin from Xingyuan, appointing him Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister, and ordered Deyu to replace Zongmin as Administrator of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong then recalled Zongmin from Xingyuan and appointed him vice director of the secretariat and chief minister, ordering Deyu to take Zongmin's place as administrator of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 既再得權位，輔之以訓、註，尤恣所欲，進封襄武侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Once he again obtained power, aided by Xun and Zhu he indulged his desires all the more; he was advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Xiangwu with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had regained power, with Xun and Zhu at his side he indulged his desires as never before; he was advanced in rank to Marquis of Xiangwu with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，京兆尹楊虞卿得罪，宗閔極言救解，文宗怒叱之曰：「爾嘗謂鄭覃是妖氣，今作妖，覃耶、爾耶？」

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year the metropolitan governor Yang Yuqing fell afoul of the law, and Zongmin spoke out forcefully in his defense. Emperor Wenzong angrily rebuked him: "You once said Zheng Tan was a baleful presence. Now a baleful one has appeared; is it Tan, or is it you?"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year the metropolitan governor Yang Yuqing fell afoul of the law, and Zongmin spoke out forcefully in his defense. Emperor Wenzong angrily rebuked him: "You once said Zheng Tan was a baleful presence. Now a baleful one has appeared; is it Tan, or is it you?"

sentences.zh: 翌日，貶明州刺史，尋再貶處州長史。

translations.literal: The next day he was demoted to Prefect of Mingzhou, and soon was demoted again to Senior Administrator of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was demoted to prefect of Mingzhou, and soon afterward was demoted again to senior administrator of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 七月，鄭註發沈、宋若憲事，內官楊承和、韋元素、沈及若憲姻黨坐貶者十餘人，又貶宗閔潮州司戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Zheng Zhu exposed the affair of Shen and Song Ruoxian; the inner officials Yang Chenghe, Wei Yuansu, Shen, and more than ten of Ruoxian's affinal kin were demoted on account of it, and Zongmin was again demoted to Registrar of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zheng Zhu exposed the affair involving Shen and Song Ruoxian. The inner officials Yang Chenghe, Wei Yuansu, and Shen, together with more than ten of Ruoxian's kin by marriage, were demoted in connection with it, and Zongmin was demoted again to registrar of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 時訓、註竊弄威權，凡不附己者，目為宗閔、德裕之黨，貶逐無虛日，中外震駭，連月陰晦，人情不安。

translations.literal: At that time Xun and Zhu usurped authority; whoever did not attach to them was labeled a partisan of Zongmin and Deyu, and demotions and banishments came day after day without pause; inside and outside the court were shaken, month after month the sky was overcast, and people's hearts were uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xun and Zhu wielded power in secret. Anyone who would not join them was branded a partisan of Zongmin or Deyu, and demotions and banishments followed day after day without respite. Court and country were shaken, the skies stayed overcast for months on end, and the mood of the people grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 九月詔曰：

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict declared:

sentences.zh: 朕承天纘歷，燭理不明，勞虛襟以求賢，勵寬德以容眾。

translations.literal: We have received Heaven's succession and illumined governance is not clear; We have wearied Our open breast to seek the worthy and encouraged broad virtue to embrace the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: We have received Heaven's mandate to rule, yet Our governance still lacks clarity. We have opened Our heart in labor to seek the worthy and encouraged magnanimity to embrace the multitude.

sentences.zh: 頃者，或臺輔乖弼違之道，而具僚扇朋附之風；

translations.literal: Recently, some at the highest levels have departed from the way of aiding and correcting, while the full corps of officials has fanned the wind of factional attachment;
translations.idiomatic: Recently some among the highest ministers have strayed from the path of loyal counsel, while the full body of officials has fanned the wind of factional attachment;

sentences.zh: 翕然相從，實篸彜憲。

translations.literal: They have rushed to follow one another, truly piercing the constant statutes.
translations.idiomatic: They have rushed to follow one another, truly piercing the foundations of law and ritual.

sentences.zh: 致使薰蕕共器，賢不肖並馳；

translations.literal: This has caused fragrant and foul to share the same vessel, the worthy and unworthy to run together;
translations.idiomatic: This has caused the fragrant and the foul to share the same vessel, the worthy and the unworthy to advance side by side;

sentences.zh: 退跡者成後時之夫，登門者有迎吠之客。

translations.literal: Those who withdrew became men behind the times, while those who entered doors had guests who barked in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Those who withdrew from office were treated as men out of step with the times, while those who came to their doors were met with the fawning of sycophants.

sentences.zh: 繆戾之氣，堙郁和平，而望陰陽順時，疵癘不作；

translations.literal: Perverse and rebellious qi has choked off harmony, yet We still hope that yin and yang will follow their seasons and that pestilence will not arise;
translations.idiomatic: Perverse and rebellious forces have choked off harmony, yet We still hope that yin and yang will keep to their seasons and that pestilence will not arise;

sentences.zh: 朝廷清肅，班列和安，自古及今，未嘗有也。

translations.literal: that the court will be pure and solemn and the ranks harmonious and at peace—from antiquity to the present there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: that the court will be pure and solemn and the official ranks harmonious and at peace—from antiquity to the present, nothing of the kind has ever been seen.

sentences.zh: 今既再申朝典，一變澆風，掃清朋比之徒，匡飭貞廉之俗。

translations.literal: Now We have again proclaimed the court statutes, transformed the corrupt custom at a stroke, swept away the factional cliques, and rectified the custom of integrity and probity.
translations.idiomatic: Now We have again proclaimed the statutes of the court, transformed the corrupt custom at a stroke, swept away the factional cliques, and restored the custom of integrity and probity.

sentences.zh: 凡百卿士，惟新令猷。

translations.literal: Let all you ministers renew your excellent plans.
translations.idiomatic: Let all you ministers renew your excellent counsel.

sentences.zh: 如聞周行之中，尚蓄疑懼，或有妄相指目，令不自安，今斯曠然，明喻朕意。

translations.literal: We have heard that among the full court there still remain suspicion and fear, and that some recklessly point fingers at others, making them uneasy. Now this is made broadly clear, and Our intent is plainly explained.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that among the full court suspicion and fear still linger, and that some recklessly point fingers at others and leave them ill at ease. Let this now be made broadly clear, and let Our intent be plainly understood.

sentences.zh: 應與宗閔、德裕或親或故及門生舊吏等，除今日已前黜遠之外，一切不問。

translations.literal: All who are kin or old associates of Zongmin and Deyu, as well as their students and former subordinates, apart from those already banished before today, are not to be questioned in any matter.
translations.idiomatic: All who are related to Zongmin or Deyu by kinship or old ties, as well as their students and former subordinates, are not to be questioned in any matter, except for those already banished before today.

sentences.zh: 各安職業，勿復為嫌。

translations.literal: Each should rest secure in his office and no longer harbor suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Let each rest secure in his office and harbor suspicion no more.

sentences.zh: 文宗以二李朋黨，繩之不能去，嘗謂侍臣曰：「去河北賊非難，去此朋黨實難。」

translations.literal: Because of the factions led by the two Lis, Emperor Wenzong could not eliminate them even when he tried to restrain them by law. He once told his attending ministers, "Driving out the rebels of Hebei is not difficult; driving out these factions truly is."
translations.idiomatic: Because of the factions led by the two Lis, Emperor Wenzong could not eliminate them even when he tried to restrain them by law. He once told his attending ministers, "Driving out the rebels of Hebei is not difficult; driving out these factions truly is."

sentences.zh: 宗閔雖驟放黜，竟免李訓之禍，

translations.literal: Although Zongmin was suddenly dismissed and banished, in the end he escaped the disaster of Li Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zongmin had been suddenly dismissed and banished, in the end he escaped the catastrophe of Li Xun's plot.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，量移衢州司馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng, He was transferred by degree to Defender of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaicheng, He was transferred under commuted sentence to defender of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，楊嗣復輔政，與宗閔厚善，欲拔用之，而畏鄭覃沮議，乃托中人密諷於上。

translations.literal: In the third year Yang Sifu assisted in government; he was on close terms with Zongmin and wished to promote and employ him, but feared Zheng Tan's obstructive counsel, and so entrusted a eunuch to hint secretly to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yang Sifu was assisting in government. He was on close terms with Zongmin and wished to promote him, but feared obstruction from Zheng Tan and therefore had a eunuch drop a private hint to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上以嗣復故，因紫宸對，謂宰相曰：「宗閔在外四五年，宜別授一官。」

translations.literal: For Sifu's sake, at an audience in the Zichen Hall the emperor told the chief ministers, "Zongmin has been away from court for four or five years. He ought to be given another office."
translations.idiomatic: For Sifu's sake, at an audience in the Zichen Hall the emperor told the chief ministers, "Zongmin has been away from court for four or five years. He ought to be given another office."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「陛下憐其地遠，宜移近內地三五百里，不可再用奸邪。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said, "Your Majesty pities him for being far away; he should be moved within three to five hundred li of the inner regions, but wicked men must not be employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "Your Majesty pities him for being so far away; he may be moved three to five hundred li nearer the heartland, but such a wicked man must not be employed again.

sentences.zh: 陛下若欲用宗閔，臣請先退。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to employ Zongmin, this subject asks to withdraw first."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to employ Zongmin, I ask to withdraw first."

sentences.zh: 陳夷行曰：「比者，宗閔得罪，以朋黨之故，恕死為幸。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing said, "Recently Zongmin offended the law on account of factionalism; to be spared death was already fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing said, "Not long ago Zongmin offended the law because of factionalism. That he was spared death was already a great mercy.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，李續之、張又新、蘇景胤等，朋比奸險，幾傾朝廷，時號『八關十六子』。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli reign Li Xuzhi, Zhang Youxin, Su Jingyin, and others formed a faction of wicked and treacherous men and nearly overturned the court; at the time they were called the Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoli reign Li Xuzhi, Zhang Youxin, Su Jingyin, and others banded together in a treacherous faction that nearly brought down the court; at the time they were known as the Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「主此事者，罪在逢吉。

translations.literal: Li Jue said, "The one chiefly responsible for this affair—his guilt lies with Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "The man chiefly responsible for this affair is Fengji; the guilt is his.

sentences.zh: 李續之居喪服闋，不可不與一官，臣恐中外衣冠，交興議論，非為續之輩也。」

translations.literal: Li Xuzhi has completed mourning; he cannot but be given some office. I fear that gentlemen inside and outside the court will all raise discussion—not on behalf of Xuzhi and his like."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuzhi has completed his mourning period and cannot be denied some office altogether. I fear that officials throughout the court and country will raise a storm of discussion—and not on behalf of Xuzhi and his like alone."

sentences.zh: 夷行曰：「昔舜逐四兇天下治。

translations.literal: Yixing said, "In antiquity Shun drove out the Four Evils and the realm was governed.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said, "In antiquity, when Shun drove out the Four Evils, the realm was well governed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷求理，何惜此十數纖人？」

translations.literal: The court seeks good order—why spare these dozen petty men?"
translations.idiomatic: The court seeks good order—why spare these dozen petty men?"

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「事貴得中，不可但徇憎愛。」

translations.literal: Sifu said, "In affairs what is valued is hitting the mean; one cannot simply follow hatred and affection."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "In affairs what matters is hitting the mean; one cannot simply follow personal hatred or favor."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「與一郡可也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Giving him one prefecture would do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Giving him a prefecture would be enough."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「與郡太優，止可洪州司馬耳。」

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said, "A prefecture is too generous; he can only be Defender of Hongzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "A prefecture is too generous. Defender of Hongzhou is all he deserves."

sentences.zh: 夷行曰：「宗閔養成鄭註之惡，幾覆邦家，國之巨蠹也。」

translations.literal: Yixing said, "Zongmin nurtured the evil of Zheng Zhu and nearly overturned the state; he is a great pest of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said, "Zongmin nurtured the evil of Zheng Zhu and nearly brought the state to ruin. He is a great pest upon the realm."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「比者，陛下欲加鄭註官，宗閔不肯，陛下亦當記憶。」

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Recently when Your Majesty wished to promote Zheng Zhu in office, Zongmin refused; Your Majesty should also remember this."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "Not long ago, when Your Majesty wished to promote Zheng Zhu in office, Zongmin refused. Your Majesty ought to remember that as well."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「嗣復黨庇宗閔。

translations.literal: Tan said, "Sifu is shielding Zongmin as a partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "Sifu is shielding Zongmin out of factional loyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣觀宗閔之惡，甚於李林甫。」

translations.literal: This subject observes that Zongmin's wickedness surpasses that of Li Linfu."
translations.idiomatic: In my view Zongmin's wickedness surpasses even that of Li Linfu."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「覃語大過。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Tan's words go too far.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "Tan has gone much too far.

sentences.zh: 昔玄宗季年，委用林甫，妒賢害能，破人家族。

translations.literal: In the late years of Emperor Xuanzong he entrusted power to Linfu, who was jealous of the worthy and harmed the capable, destroying families.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Emperor Xuanzong he entrusted power to Linfu, who was jealous of the worthy and harmed the capable and destroyed whole families.

sentences.zh: 宗閔在位，固無此事。

translations.literal: When Zongmin held office, there was certainly nothing of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongmin held office, nothing of that kind occurred.

sentences.zh: 況太和末，宗閔、德裕同時得罪。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the end of the Taihe era Zongmin and Deyu both offended the law at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the end of the Taihe era Zongmin and Deyu both fell afoul of the law at the same time.

sentences.zh: 二年之間，德裕再領重鎮，而宗閔未離貶所。

translations.literal: Within two years Deyu again took command of a major defense post, while Zongmin had not left his place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years Deyu had again taken command of a major military region, while Zongmin had not yet left his place of banishment.

sentences.zh: 陛下懲惡勸善，進退之理宜均，非臣獨敢黨庇。

translations.literal: Your Majesty punishes evil and encourages good; the principle of advancement and withdrawal ought to be even—it is not that this subject alone dares to shield a partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty punishes evil and encourages good. The principle governing advancement and dismissal ought to be evenhanded. It is not that I alone dare to shield a partisan.

sentences.zh: 昨殷侑與韓益奏官及章服，臣以益前年犯贓，未可其奏；

translations.literal: Yesterday Yin You and Han Yi memorialized regarding office and ceremonial robes; this subject held that Yi had committed embezzlement the year before last and their memorial could not be approved;
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday Yin You and Han Yi memorialized regarding office and ceremonial robes. I held that Yi had committed embezzlement the year before last and that their memorial could not be approved;

sentences.zh: 鄭覃托臣雲『幸且勿論。』

translations.literal: Zheng Tan entrusted this subject, saying, 'For now let us not discuss it.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan asked me, saying, 'For now let us not discuss it.'

sentences.zh: 孰為黨庇？」

translations.literal: Who is shielding a partisan?"
translations.idiomatic: Who, then, is shielding a partisan?"

sentences.zh: 翌日，以宗閔為杭州刺史。

translations.literal: The next day Zongmin was appointed Prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zongmin was appointed prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，遷太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year he was transferred to mentor of the heir apparent with duty at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 時鄭覃、陳夷行罷相，嗣復方再拔用宗閔知政事，俄而文宗崩。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Tan and Chen Yixing were removed as chief ministers; Sifu was just about to promote Zongmin again to share in governing affairs when suddenly Emperor Wenzong died.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Tan and Chen Yixing had been removed as chief ministers, and Sifu was on the point of promoting Zongmin again to share in governing affairs when suddenly Emperor Wenzong died.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，李德裕秉政，嗣復、李玨皆竄嶺表。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huichang era Li Deyu held power; Sifu and Li Jue were both banished to the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huichang era Deyu held power, and both Sifu and Li Jue were banished to the far south.

sentences.zh: 三年，劉稹據澤潞叛。

translations.literal: In the third year Liu Zhen held Ze and Lu in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Liu Zhen rebelled and held Ze and Lu.

sentences.zh: 德裕以宗閔素與劉從諫厚，上黨近東都，宗閔分司非便，出為封州刺史。

translations.literal: Deyu, because Zongmin had long been on close terms with Liu Congjian and because Shangdang was near the Eastern Capital, held that it was not appropriate for Zongmin to hold duty there; he was sent out as Prefect of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu, noting that Zongmin had long been on close terms with Liu Congjian and that Shangdang lay near the eastern capital, held that it was inappropriate for Zongmin to remain on duty there and had him sent out as prefect of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 又發其舊事，貶郴州司馬，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: His old affairs were again exposed, and he was demoted to Defender of Chenzhou, dying in his place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: His old affairs were exposed again, and he was demoted to defender of Chenzhou, where he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 子琨、瓚，大中朝皆進士擢第。

translations.literal: His sons Kun and Zan both passed the jinshi examination in the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Kun and Zan both passed the jinshi examination during the Dazhong reign.

sentences.zh: 令狐綯作相，特加獎拔。

translations.literal: When Linghu Tao became chief minister, he gave them special encouragement and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Tao became chief minister, he singled them out for encouragement and promotion.

sentences.zh: 瓚自員外郎知制誥，歷中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: Zan, from Vice Director as drafter of edicts, passed through Attendant Drafting at the Secretariat and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Zan rose from vice director as drafter of edicts to attendant drafting at the secretariat and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 綯罷相，出為桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: When Tao left the chief ministership, Zan went out as Observation Commissioner of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao left office as chief minister, Zan was sent out as observation commissioner of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 御軍無政，為卒所逐，貶死。

translations.literal: He governed the army without discipline and was driven out by the soldiers; he was demoted and died.
translations.idiomatic: He governed his troops without discipline and was driven out by his soldiers; he was demoted and died.

sentences.zh: 自天寶艱難之後，宗室子弟，賢而立功者，唯鄭王、曹王子孫耳。

translations.literal: Since the hardships of the Tianbao era, among imperial clansmen who were worthy and established achievement, there were only the descendants of the Princes of Zheng and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Since the hardships of the Tianbao era, among members of the imperial clan who were worthy and achieved distinction, only the descendants of the Princes of Zheng and Cao remained.

sentences.zh: 夷簡再從季父汧國公勉，德宗朝宰相。

translations.literal: Yijian's second cousin once removed was the Prince of Qian, Li Mian, chief minister in the Dezong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian's second cousin once removed was Li Mian, Prince of Qian, who had been chief minister under Emperor Dezong.

sentences.zh: 夷簡諸弟夷亮、夷則、夷範，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: Yijian's younger brothers Yiliang, Yize, and Yifan all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian's younger brothers Yiliang, Yize, and Yifan all passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 宗閔弟宗冉。

translations.literal: Zongmin's younger brother was Zongran.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin's younger brother was Zongran.

sentences.zh: 宗冉子深、湯。

translations.literal: Zongran's sons were Shen and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Zongran had sons named Shen and Tang.

sentences.zh: 湯累官至給事中，咸通中踐更臺閣，知名於時。

translations.literal: Tang rose through offices to Grand Master of Remonstrance; in the Xiantong era he served in succession at the court departments and was well known in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Tang rose through the ranks to grand master of remonstrance, and during the Xiantong reign he served in successive posts at the central court, where he became well known.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣復，字繼之，僕射於陵子也。

translations.literal: Yang Sifu, courtesy name Jizhi, was the son of Vice Chancellor Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu, whose courtesy name was Jizhi, was the son of Vice Chancellor Yang Yuling.

sentences.zh: 初，於陵十九登進十第，二十再登博學宏詞科，謂補潤州句容尉。

translations.literal: At first, at nineteen Yuling passed the jinshi examination; at twenty he again passed the Bogu Hongci decree examination, and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Jurong in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Yuling passed the jinshi examination at nineteen, and at twenty he again passed the erudite literature decree examination, after which he was appointed assistant magistrate of Jurong county in Run prefecture.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使韓滉有知人之鑒，見之甚悅。

translations.literal: Han Huang, Military Commissioner of Zhexi, had a gift for judging men; on meeting him he was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, the military commissioner of Zhexi, had a keen eye for talent, and he was greatly pleased when he met Yuling.

sentences.zh: 滉有愛女，方擇佳婿，謂其妻柳氏曰：「吾閱人多矣，無如楊生貴而有壽，生子必為宰相。」

translations.literal: Huang had a beloved daughter and was choosing a suitable son-in-law; he said to his wife, Lady Liu: "I have reviewed many men, but none like Young Master Yang—he is noble and will live long, and his son will surely become chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Huang had a beloved daughter and was choosing a suitable son-in-law; he said to his wife, Lady Liu: "I have reviewed many men, but none like Young Master Yang—he is noble and will live long, and his son will surely become chief minister."

sentences.zh: 於陵秩滿，寓居揚州而生嗣復。

translations.literal: Yuling's term of office ended; residing in Yangzhou he fathered Sifu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuling's term of office ended, he took up residence in Yangzhou, where Sifu was born.

sentences.zh: 後滉見之，撫其首曰：「名位果逾於父，楊門之慶也。」

translations.literal: Later, when Huang saw him, he stroked his head and said: "Your rank and office truly surpass your father's—the good fortune of the Yang house."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Huang saw him, he stroked his head and said: "Your rank and office truly surpass your father's—the good fortune of the Yang house."

sentences.zh: 因字曰慶門。

translations.literal: He then gave him the courtesy name Qingmen.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him the courtesy name Qingmen, "Gate of Good Fortune."

sentences.zh: 嗣復七八歲時已能秉筆為文。

translations.literal: When Sifu was seven or eight years old he could already take up the brush and compose writing.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of seven or eight, Sifu could already take up the brush and write.

sentences.zh: 年二十，進士擢第。

translations.literal: At age twenty he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 二十一，又登博學宏詞科，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: At twenty-one he again passed the Bogu Hongci decree examination, put aside coarse cloth, and became Proofreader at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-one he also passed the erudite literature decree examination and entered official service as a proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷右拾遺，直史館。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Reminder and served at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right reminder and appointed to serve at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 以嗣復深於禮學，改太常博士，

translations.literal: Because Sifu was deeply versed in the study of rites, he was changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices,
translations.idiomatic: Because Sifu was deeply versed in ritual studies, he was reassigned as an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，累遷至刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe, was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanhe, He was then promoted in succession to vice director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶為詳定禮儀使，奏為判官，改禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuqing served as Commissioner for the Detailed Fixing of Ritual Usages; he memorialized to have him as a case officer, and he was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yuqing served as commissioner for the detailed fixing of ritual usages, he recommended Sifu as his case officer, and Sifu was reassigned as vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時父於陵為戶部侍郎，嗣復上言與父同省非便，請換他官。

translations.literal: At the time his father Yuling was Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; Sifu submitted a memorial saying that serving in the same ministry as his father was unsuitable, and requested transfer to another office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his father Yuling was vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, and Sifu submitted a memorial arguing that serving in the same ministry as his father was improper and asking to be transferred to another post.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「應同司官有大功以下親者，但非連判及勾檢之官並官長，則不在回避之限。

translations.literal: An edict said: "For officials of the same bureau who have relatives within the degree of great-great-grandparent, only if they are not jointly serving as case officers or auditing officers, nor as bureau chiefs, are they not within the limits of avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Officials of the same bureau who have relatives within the degree of great-great-grandparent need not observe avoidance unless they serve jointly as case officers or auditing officers, or unless one holds the chief post in the bureau.

sentences.zh: 如官署同，職司異，雖父子兄弟無所避嫌。」

translations.literal: If they belong to the same office but hold different duties, even fathers and sons or brothers need not observe avoidance."
translations.idiomatic: If they belong to the same office but hold different duties, even fathers and sons or brothers need not observe avoidance."

sentences.zh: 再遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted again to director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年十月，以庫部郎中知制誥，正拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, in the tenth month, as Director of the Ministry of State Treasury he served as Director of Drafting; he was formally appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing, in the tenth month he served as director of the Ministry of State Treasury with charge of drafting edicts, and was formally appointed a secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 嗣復與牛僧孺、李宗閔皆權德輿貢舉門生，情義相得，進退取舍，多與之同。

translations.literal: Sifu, Niu Sengru, and Li Zongmin were all examination graduates of Quan Deyu; in mutual affection they agreed, and in advancement, withdrawal, accepting and rejecting, they mostly agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu, Niu Sengru, and Li Zongmin had all been examination graduates under Quan Deyu; they were bound by mutual affection, and in advancement, withdrawal, and political choices they mostly followed his lead.

sentences.zh: 四年，僧孺作相，欲薦拔大用，又以於陵為東都留守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Sengru became chief minister and wished to recommend and promote him for major use, but as Yuling was Eastern Capital Regent, he had not yet held the chief ministership, and so Sifu was appointed acting Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Sengru became chief minister, he wished to recommend Sifu for major appointment, but because Yuling was serving as regent of the eastern capital and had not yet held the chief ministership, Sifu was instead appointed acting vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 未歷相位，乃令嗣復權知禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Not having yet held the rank of chief minister, he had Sifu act as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Since Sifu had not yet served as chief minister, Sengru had him serve as acting vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 寶曆元年二月，選貢士六十八人，後多至達官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli, in the second month he selected sixty-eight tribute students; many later reached high offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli, in the second month he selected sixty-eight examination candidates, many of whom later rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Sifu was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Sifu was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以父於陵太子少傅致仕，年高多疾，懇辭侍養，不之許，

translations.literal: Because his father Yuling had retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, was advanced in years and often ill, he earnestly declined to serve so he could attend and support him; this was not granted,
translations.idiomatic: Because his father Yuling had retired as junior tutor to the heir apparent and, being advanced in years and often ill, Sifu earnestly asked to be relieved of duty so he could care for him, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，丁父憂免。

translations.literal: In Taihe year four, he entered mourning upon his father's death and was relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year four, he entered mourning upon his father's death and was relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，起為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year he was recalled to serve as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year he was recalled to serve as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 其年宗閔罷相，德裕輔政。

translations.literal: That year Zongmin was removed as chief minister and Deyu assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Zongmin was dismissed as chief minister, and Li Deyu took up a leading role in government.

sentences.zh: 七月，以嗣復檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Sifu was made titular Director of the Ministry of Rites, Prefect of Zizhou, and Military Commissioner and Observer of Jiannan East Circuit, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Sifu was appointed titular director of the Ministry of Rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military commissioner and observer of Jiannan East Circuit, among other posts.

sentences.zh: 九年，宗閔復知政事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Zongmin again handled governmental affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Zongmin again took charge of governmental affairs.

sentences.zh: 三月，以嗣復檢校戶部尚書、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使知節度事、觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the third month Sifu was made titular Director of the Ministry of Revenue, Prefect of Chengdu, Deputy Military Commissioner knowing circuit affairs of Jiannan West Circuit, and Commissioner for Observation and Disposition, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Sifu was appointed titular director of the Ministry of Revenue, prefect of Chengdu, deputy military commissioner in charge of Jiannan West Circuit affairs, and commissioner for observation and disposition, among other posts.

sentences.zh: 開成二年十月，入為戶部侍郎，領諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng, in the tenth month he entered the capital as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and headed the Salt and Iron Transport Commission for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaicheng, in the tenth month he was recalled to the capital as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and appointed head of the salt and iron transport commission for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，與同列李玨並以本官同平章事，領使如故，進階金紫，弘農伯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, he and his colleague Li Jue were both appointed Grand Counselors with their existing offices, retaining their commissionerships as before; he was advanced to golden-purple rank, made Baron of Hongnong, with an estate of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he and his colleague Li Jue were both appointed grand counselors while retaining their existing posts, and Sifu was promoted to golden-purple rank and created baron of Hongnong with an estate of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 上以幣輕錢重，問鹽鐵使何以去其太甚？

translations.literal: The emperor, because silk currency was light and coin heavy, asked the Salt and Iron Commissioner how to remove the excess?
translations.idiomatic: Because silk currency was undervalued relative to coin, the emperor asked the salt and iron commissioner how to correct the imbalance?

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「此事累朝制置未得，但且禁銅，未可變法。

translations.literal: Sifu said: "This matter successive courts have arranged without success; for now only ban copper—it is not yet possible to change the law.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "Successive courts have tried to address this without success; for now we should only enforce the ban on copper—it is not yet possible to change the law.

sentences.zh: 法變擾人，終亦未罷去弊。」

translations.literal: Changing the law would disturb the people, and in the end the underlying abuse would still not be eliminated."
translations.idiomatic: Changing the law would disturb the people, and in the end the underlying abuse would still not be eliminated."

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「禁銅之令，朝廷常典，但行之不嚴，不如無令。

translations.literal: Li Jue said: "The order banning copper is a regular statute of the court, but if it is not enforced strictly, it would be better to have no order.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said: "The ban on copper is a standing statute of the court, but if it is not enforced strictly, it would be better to have no ban at all.

sentences.zh: 今江淮已南，銅器成肆，市井逐利者，銷錢一緡，可為數器，售利三四倍。

translations.literal: Now south of the Yangtze and Huai, copperware shops have formed; market profiteers melt one string of cash into several vessels and sell them for three or four times the profit.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze and Huai, copperware shops now line the streets, and market profiteers melt a single string of cash into several vessels that they sell for three or four times the profit.

sentences.zh: 遠民不知法令，率以為常。

translations.literal: People in distant regions do not know the laws and decrees, and generally take this as normal.
translations.idiomatic: People in outlying regions do not know the law and generally treat this as normal practice.

sentences.zh: 縱國家加爐鑄錢，何以供銷鑄之弊？

translations.literal: Even if the state increases furnaces and casts coin, how can it supply the abuse of melting and casting?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the state increased its minting, how could it keep pace with the abuse of illegal melting?

sentences.zh: 所以禁銅之令，不得不嚴。」

translations.literal: Therefore the order banning copper cannot but be strict."
translations.idiomatic: That is why the ban on copper must be strictly enforced."

sentences.zh: 八月，紫宸奏事，曰：「聖人在上，野無遺賢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, at Zichen Hall reporting affairs, he said: "With a sage on the throne, no worthy in the wilds is overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, at Zichen Hall, Sifu reported on affairs and said: "With a sage on the throne, no worthy talent in the land should be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 陸洿上疏論兵，雖不中時事，意亦可獎。

translations.literal: Lu Fu submitted a memorial discussing military affairs; although it did not fit the times, the intent is also praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fu had submitted a memorial on military affairs; although it was not timely, his intent was still praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 閑居蘇州累年，宜與一官。」

translations.literal: He has lived in retirement in Suzhou for many years and should be granted an official appointment."
translations.idiomatic: He has lived in retirement in Suzhou for many years and should be granted an official appointment."

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「士子趨競者多，若獎陸洿，貪夫知勸矣。

translations.literal: Li Jue said: "Many scholars vie and compete; if Lu Fu is rewarded, the greedy will know encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said: "Many scholars are eager to compete for favor; if Lu Fu is rewarded, the greedy will take it as encouragement.

sentences.zh: 昨竇洵直論事，陛下賞之以幣帛，況與陸洿官耶？」

translations.literal: Yesterday, when Dou Xunzhi spoke out on policy, Your Majesty rewarded him with silk and cloth—how much more readily would an office be granted to Lu Fu?"
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, when Dou Xunzhi spoke out on policy, Your Majesty rewarded him with silk and cloth—how much more readily would an office be granted to Lu Fu?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「洵直獎其直心，不言事之當否。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Xunzhi was rewarded for his frankness, not for whether his views were right or wrong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Xunzhi was rewarded for his frankness, not for whether his views were right or wrong."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「若苞藏則不可知。」

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "If one harbors hidden motives, that cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said: "If one harbors hidden motives, that cannot be known."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「臣深知洵直無邪惡，所奏陸洿官，尚未奉聖旨。」

translations.literal: Sifu said: "I know well that Xunzhi has no evil intent, and the memorial I submitted to grant Lu Fu an office has not yet received Your Majesty's approval."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "I know well that Xunzhi has no evil intent, and the memorial I submitted to grant Lu Fu an office has not yet received Your Majesty's approval."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「陛下須防朋黨。」

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "Your Majesty must guard against factions."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said: "Your Majesty must guard against factions."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「鄭覃疑臣朋黨，乞陛下放臣歸去。」

translations.literal: Sifu said: "Zheng Tan suspects me of factionalism; I beg Your Majesty to let me return home."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "Zheng Tan suspects me of factionalism; I beg Your Majesty to let me return home."

sentences.zh: 因拜乞罷免。

translations.literal: He then bowed and begged to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He then bowed and begged to be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「比來朋黨，近亦稍弭。」

translations.literal: Li Jue said: "Factions have also gradually subsided in recent times."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said: "Factions have also gradually subsided in recent times."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「近有小朋黨生。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "Recently a small faction has arisen."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "Recently a small faction has arisen."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此輩雕喪向盡。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That crowd is nearly spent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That crowd is nearly spent."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「楊漢公、張又新、李續之即今尚在。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "Yang Hangong, Zhang Youxin, and Li Xuzhi are still alive today."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "Yang Hangong, Zhang Youxin, and Li Xuzhi are still alive today."

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「今有邊事論奏。」

translations.literal: Jue said: "There are now frontier matters to report on."
translations.idiomatic: Jue said: "There are now frontier matters to report on."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「論邊事安危，臣不如玨；

translations.literal: Tan said: "In discussing frontier affairs, safety and peril, your subject is not as good as Jue;
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "When it comes to discussing frontier affairs and their dangers, I am not Jue's equal;

sentences.zh: 嫉惡則玨不如臣。」

translations.literal: but in hating evil, Jue is not my equal."
translations.idiomatic: but in hating evil, Jue is not my equal."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「臣聞左右佩劍，彼此相笑。

translations.literal: Sifu said: "Your subject has heard that when left and right wear swords, they laugh at each other.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "I have heard that when two men at court both wear swords, each laughs at the other.

sentences.zh: 臣今不知鄭覃指誰為朋黨。」

translations.literal: I do not yet know whom Zheng Tan is calling a faction."
translations.idiomatic: I do not yet know whom Zheng Tan is calling a faction."

sentences.zh: 因當香案前奏曰：「臣待罪宰相，不能申夔、龍之道，唯以朋黨見譏，必乞陛下罷臣鼎職。」

translations.literal: He then submitted before the incense table and said: "I serve as chief minister under a charge of guilt, yet I cannot uphold the way of Kui and Long; I am accused only of factionalism, and I must beg Your Majesty to dismiss me from the chief ministership."
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted before the incense table and said: "I serve as chief minister under a charge of guilt, yet I cannot uphold the way of Kui and Long; I am accused only of factionalism, and I must beg Your Majesty to dismiss me from the chief ministership."

sentences.zh: 上慰勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted and urged him to remain.

sentences.zh: 文宗方以政事委嗣復，惡覃言切。

translations.literal: Wenzong was then entrusting governmental affairs to Sifu and disliked Tan's cutting words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was at this time entrusting governmental affairs to Sifu and resented Tan's sharp remarks.

sentences.zh: 帝延英謂宰臣曰：「人傳符讖之語，自何而來？」

translations.literal: At Yanying Hall the emperor said to the chief ministers: "People circulate prophecies and omens—where do such words come from?"
translations.idiomatic: At Yanying Hall the emperor said to the chief ministers: "People circulate prophecies and omens—where do such words come from?"

sentences.zh: 嗣復對曰：「漢光武好以讖書決事，近代隋文帝亦信此言，自是，此說日滋，只如班彪《王命論》所引，蓋矯意以止賊亂，非所重也。」

translations.literal: Sifu replied: "Emperor Guangwu of Han liked to decide affairs by prophecy texts, and in recent times Emperor Wen of Sui also believed such words. Since then the doctrine has spread daily. Even what Ban Biao's Discourse on the Mandate of Kingship cites was surely a feigned argument to stop rebellion, not something to be taken seriously."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu replied: "Emperor Guangwu of Han liked to decide affairs by prophecy texts, and in recent times Emperor Wen of Sui also believed such words. Since then the doctrine has spread daily. Even what Ban Biao's Discourse on the Mandate of Kingship cites was surely a feigned argument to stop rebellion, not something to be taken seriously."

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「喪亂之時，佐命者務神符命；

translations.literal: Li Jue said: "In times of calamity and disorder, those who assist the mandate strive for divine tally-mandates;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said: "In times of calamity and disorder, those who assist a new mandate appeal to divine portents;

sentences.zh: 理平之代，只合推諸人事。」

translations.literal: in an age of peace and good order, one should rely only on human effort."
translations.idiomatic: in an age of peace and good order, one should rely only on human effort."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What you say is right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What you say is right."

sentences.zh: 帝又曰：「天後用人，有自布衣至宰相者，當時還得力否？」

translations.literal: The emperor also said: "When the Heavenly Empress appointed men, some rose from commoner status to chief minister—were they effective at the time?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said: "When the Heavenly Empress appointed men, some rose from commoner status to chief minister—were they effective at the time?"

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「天後重行刑辟，輕用官爵，皆自圖之計耳。

translations.literal: Sifu replied: "The Empress Dowager stressed punishments and lightly used offices and enfeoffments—all schemes for her own advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu replied: "The Empress Dowager emphasized punishments and used offices and enfeoffments lightly—all schemes for her own advantage.

sentences.zh: 凡用人之道，歷試方見其能否。

translations.literal: As for the way of employing men, only after repeated testing can one's capacity be seen.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, one can tell whether a man is capable only after testing him over time.

sentences.zh: 當艱難之時，或須拔擢，無事之日，不如且循資級。

translations.literal: In times of hardship one may need to promote specially; in days without affairs, it is better for now to follow seniority grades.
translations.idiomatic: In difficult times exceptional promotion may be necessary, but in peaceful times it is better to advance men by seniority.

sentences.zh: 古人拔卒為將，非治平之時，蓋不獲已而用之也。」

translations.literal: When the ancients promoted soldiers to generals, they did so not in well-governed times but only when they had no other choice."
translations.idiomatic: When the ancients promoted soldiers to generals, they did so not in well-governed times but only when they had no other choice."

sentences.zh: 上又問新修《開元政要》，敘致何如。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked about the newly compiled "Essential Policies of the Kaiyuan Era"—how was its exposition?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked about the newly compiled "Essential Policies of the Kaiyuan Era" and how well it was written.

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「臣等未見。

translations.literal: Sifu said: "We your subjects have not seen it.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "We have not yet seen it.

sentences.zh: 陛下若欲遺之子孫，則請宣付臣等，參詳可否。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to bequeath it to descendants, then please deliver it to us your subjects to examine whether it is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty intends to leave it to posterity, please deliver it to us so that we may review whether it is suitable.

sentences.zh: 玄宗或好遊畋，或好聲色，與貞觀之政不同，故取舍須當，方堪流傳。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong sometimes loved hunting, sometimes loved sound and color—it differs from the government of the Zhenguan era, so selection must be proper before it can be handed down."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong sometimes indulged in hunting and sometimes in music and women, so his reign differed from the Zhenguan era; selections must therefore be made with care if the work is to endure."

sentences.zh: 四年五月，上問延英政事，逐日何人記錄監修？

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year the emperor asked who recorded and supervised the daily Yingying Hall governmental affairs?
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year the emperor asked who was responsible for recording and supervising the daily deliberations at Yingying Hall?

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「是臣職司。」

translations.literal: Li Jue said: "That is my duty."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said: "That is my duty."

sentences.zh: 陳夷行曰：「宰相所錄，必當自伐，聖德即將掩之。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing said: "What chief ministers record will surely boast of themselves—the sage virtue will soon be obscured.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing said: "What chief ministers record will surely glorify themselves, and Your Majesty's virtue will soon be obscured.

sentences.zh: 臣所以頻言，不欲威權在下。」

translations.literal: That is why I have spoken repeatedly—I do not want authority to remain vested below."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have spoken repeatedly—I do not want authority to remain vested below."

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「夷行此言，是疑宰相中有賣威權、貨刑賞者。

translations.literal: Jue said: "Yixing's words suspect that among chief ministers there are those who sell authority and power and trade punishments and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Jue said: "Yixing's words imply that among the chief ministers there are those who sell authority and trade punishments and rewards.

sentences.zh: 不然，何自為宰相而出此言？

translations.literal: Otherwise, why as a chief minister himself would he speak such words?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, why would he speak this way when he himself is a chief minister?

sentences.zh: 臣累奏求退，若得王傅，臣之幸也。」

translations.literal: I have repeatedly asked to retire; if I could become a royal tutor, I would count myself fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I have repeatedly asked to retire; if I could become a royal tutor, I would count myself fortunate."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「陛下開成元年、二年政事至好，三年、四年漸不如前。」

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "Your Majesty, government in the first and second years of Kaicheng was excellent, but in the third and fourth years it has gradually declined."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said: "Your Majesty, government in the first and second years of Kaicheng was excellent, but in the third and fourth years it has gradually declined."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「元年、二年是鄭覃、夷行用事，三年、四年臣與李玨同之。

translations.literal: Sifu said: "The first and second years were when Zheng Tan and Yixing held power; the third and fourth years your subject and Li Jue shared it.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "In the first and second years Zheng Tan and Yixing held power; in the third and fourth years Li Jue and I shared it.

sentences.zh: 臣蒙聖慈擢處相位，不能悉心奉職。

translations.literal: Your subject received the sage grace and was raised to the chief minister's seat, yet cannot fully devote heart to fulfilling duty.
translations.idiomatic: I was raised to the chief ministership by Your Majesty's grace, yet I have not been able to devote myself fully to my duties.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃云『三年之後，一年不如一年』，臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan says 'after the third year, each year is worse than the last'—that is your subject's crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Tan says that 'after the third year, each year has been worse than the last,' the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 陛下縱不誅夷，臣合自求泯滅。」

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty does not punish me, I ought to remove myself from public life."
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty does not punish me, I ought to remove myself from public life."

sentences.zh: 因叩頭曰：「臣今日便辭玉階，不敢更入中書。」

translations.literal: He then kowtowed and said: "Today I shall leave the jade steps and dare not enter the Secretariat again."
translations.idiomatic: He then kowtowed and said: "Today I shall leave the jade steps and dare not enter the Secretariat again."

sentences.zh: 即趨去。

translations.literal: He then hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: He then hurried off.

sentences.zh: 上令中使召還，勞之曰：「鄭覃失言，卿何及此？」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered an inner attendant to summon him back and comforted him, saying: "Zheng Tan misspoke—how did you come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inner attendant to summon him back and comforted him, saying: "Zheng Tan misspoke—how did you come to this?"

sentences.zh: 覃起謝曰：「臣性愚拙，言無顧慮。

translations.literal: Tan rose and apologized, saying: "Your subject's nature is dull and clumsy; his words lack consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Tan rose and apologized, saying: "My nature is dull and clumsy, and my words lack consideration.

sentences.zh: 近日事亦漸好，未免些些不公，亦無甚處。

translations.literal: Recently affairs have also gradually improved; there are unavoidably some slight injustices, but nothing very serious.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times affairs have also gradually improved. There are unavoidably a few minor injustices, but nothing very serious.

sentences.zh: 臣亦不獨斥嗣復，遽何至此。

translations.literal: Your subject also did not single out Sifu alone for blame—how did it suddenly come to this?
translations.idiomatic: I was not singling out Sifu alone for criticism—how did matters suddenly come to this?

sentences.zh: 所為若是，乃嗣復不容臣耳。」

translations.literal: If that is how he acted, it was simply that Sifu could not tolerate me."
translations.idiomatic: If that is how he acted, it was simply that Sifu could not tolerate me."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「陛下不以臣微才，用為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Sifu said: "Your Majesty, not regarding your subject's slight talent, used him as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "Your Majesty appointed me vice director of the secretariat despite my modest ability.

sentences.zh: 時政善否，其責在臣。

translations.literal: Whether current government is good or bad, the responsibility lies with your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Whether current policy succeeds or fails, the responsibility lies with me.

sentences.zh: 陛下月費俸錢數十萬，時新珍異，必先賜與，蓋欲輔佐聖明，臻於至理。

translations.literal: Your Majesty monthly spends salary money in the hundreds of thousands; fresh and rare seasonal goods are always first granted to your subject—this was surely meant to assist the sage brilliance and reach the utmost principle of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty spends hundreds of thousands each month on my salary and always sends me the season's finest rarities first. The aim was surely to help me assist Your Majesty's enlightened rule and bring governance to the highest standard.

sentences.zh: 既一年不如一年，非惟臣合得罪，亦上累聖德。

translations.literal: Since each year has been worse than the last, not only ought your subject be guilty, it also above tarnishes the sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Since each year has been worse than the last, I deserve punishment not only on my own account but also because I have reflected poorly on Your Majesty's virtue.

sentences.zh: 伏請別命賢能，許臣休退。」

translations.literal: I humbly ask that Your Majesty appoint another worthy man and allow me to retire."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty appoint another worthy man and allow me to retire."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「鄭覃之言偶然耳，奚執咎耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zheng Tan's words were merely an offhand remark—why take offense?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Zheng Tan's words were merely an offhand remark—why take offense?"

sentences.zh: 嗣復數日不入，上表請罷。

translations.literal: For several days Sifu did not enter court and submitted a memorial requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: For several days Sifu stayed away from court and submitted a memorial asking to be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 帝方委用，乃罷鄭覃、夷行知政事。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then entrusting him with use, and so dismissed Zheng Tan and Yixing from governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still relying on him, and so removed Zheng Tan and Yixing from the management of government affairs.

sentences.zh: 自是，政歸嗣復，進加門下侍郎。

translations.literal: From this, government returned to Sifu, and he was further promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: From that point government reverted to Sifu, and he was further promoted to vice director of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，文宗崩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, Emperor Wenzong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, Emperor Wenzong died.

sentences.zh: 先是，以敬宗子陳王為皇太子。

translations.literal: Before this, the Prince of Chen, a son of Emperor Jingzong, had been made crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Prince of Chen, a son of Emperor Jingzong, had been named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 中尉仇士良違遺令立武宗。

translations.literal: The commandant Qiu Shiliang violated the testamentary order and enthroned Emperor Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant Qiu Shiliang defied the late emperor's last instructions and enthroned Emperor Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 武宗之立，既非宰相本意，甚薄執政之臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong's enthronement, being contrary to the chief ministers' original intent, greatly slighted the governing officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong's enthronement had not been the chief ministers' original intent, and it greatly slighted the men then in power.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，李德裕自淮南入輔政。

translations.literal: That autumn, Li Deyu entered from Huainan to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, Deyu came from Huainan to join the government.

sentences.zh: 九月，出嗣復為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Sifu was sent out as Hunan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Sifu was sent out to serve as observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 明年，誅樞密薛季稜、劉弘逸。

translations.literal: The next year, the pivot secretaries Xue Jiling and Liu Hongyi were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the pivot secretaries Xue Jiling and Liu Hongyi were executed.

sentences.zh: 中人言：「二人頃附嗣復、李玨，不利於陛下。」

translations.literal: The inner agents said: "These two men had recently sided with Sifu and Li Jue, to Your Majesty's detriment."
translations.idiomatic: The inner agents said: "These two men had recently sided with Sifu and Li Jue, to Your Majesty's detriment."

sentences.zh: 武宗性急，立命中使往湖南、桂管，殺嗣復與玨。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong's nature was impatient; he immediately ordered envoys to Hunan and Guiguan to kill Sifu and Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong was impatient by nature and immediately ordered envoys to Hunan and Guiguan to kill Sifu and Jue.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔鄲、崔珙等亟請開延英，因極言國朝故事，大臣非惡逆顯著，未有誅戮者，願陛下復思其宜。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Cui Dan, Cui Gong, and others urgently requested that Yanying be opened and thereupon spoke at length of the dynastic precedents: no great minister who was not conspicuously wicked and rebellious had ever been put to death, and they begged Your Majesty to reconsider what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Cui Dan, Cui Gong, and others urgently asked that Yanying be opened and then cited dynastic precedent at length: no great minister who was not openly wicked and rebellious had ever been executed, and they begged the emperor to reconsider what was fitting.

sentences.zh: 帝良久改容曰：「朕纘嗣之際，宰相何嘗比數。

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor changed expression and said: "At the time of my succession, when did chief ministers count for anything?
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the emperor changed expression and said: "At the time of my succession, when did chief ministers count for anything?

sentences.zh: 李玨、季稜志在扶冊陳王，嗣復、弘逸志在樹立安王。

translations.literal: Li Jue and Jiling aimed to support enthroning the Prince of Chen; Sifu and Hongyi aimed to establish the Prince of An.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Jiling aimed to support enthroning the Prince of Chen, while Sifu and Hongyi aimed to establish the Prince of An.

sentences.zh: 立陳王猶是文宗遺旨，嗣復欲立安王，全是希楊妃意旨。

translations.literal: Enthroning the Prince of Chen was still Emperor Wenzong's testamentary wish; Sifu wanting to establish the Prince of An was entirely to win Consort Yang's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Enthroning the Prince of Chen was still in accord with Emperor Wenzong's last wishes, whereas Sifu's wish to establish the Prince of An was entirely an attempt to please Consort Yang.

sentences.zh: 嗣復嘗與妃書云：『姑姑何不敩則天臨朝？』」

translations.literal: Sifu once wrote to the consort, saying, 'Aunt, why not follow Empress Wu's example and hold court?'"
translations.idiomatic: Sifu once wrote to the consort, saying, 'Aunt, why not follow Empress Wu's example and hold court?'"

sentences.zh: 珙等曰：「此事曖昧，真虛難辨。」

translations.literal: Gong and the others said: "This matter is obscure, and truth and falsehood are hard to distinguish."
translations.idiomatic: Gong and the others said: "This matter is obscure, and truth and falsehood are hard to distinguish."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「楊妃曾臥疾，妃弟玄思，文宗令入內侍疾月餘，此時通導意旨。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Consort Yang was once bedridden; her younger brother Xuanen was ordered by Emperor Wenzong to enter the palace and attend her illness for more than a month, and at that time he conveyed and guided her wishes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Consort Yang was once bedridden. Her younger brother Xuanen was ordered by Emperor Wenzong to enter the palace and attend her illness for more than a month, and at that time he conveyed her wishes.

sentences.zh: 朕細問內人，情狀皎然，我不欲宣出於外。

translations.literal: I questioned the inner attendants in detail, and the circumstances are perfectly clear; I do not wish to make this known outside.
translations.idiomatic: I questioned the palace attendants in detail, and the circumstances are perfectly clear. I do not wish to make this known outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 向使安王得志，我豈有今日？

translations.literal: If the Prince of An had had his way, would I have today?
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince of An had had his way, would I be where I am today?

sentences.zh: 然為卿等恕之。」

translations.literal: Yet for your sake I will pardon them."
translations.idiomatic: Yet for your sake I will pardon them."

sentences.zh: 乃追潭、桂二中使，再貶嗣復潮州刺史。

translations.literal: He then recalled the two envoys to Tan and Gui and again demoted Sifu to Prefect of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then recalled the two envoys bound for Tan and Gui and again demoted Sifu to prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，徵拜吏部尚書，

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Sifu was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel,
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Sifu was summoned and appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 大中二年，自潮陽還，至岳州病，一日而卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong, returning from Chaoyang, at Yuezhou he fell ill and died after one day, at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong, on his return from Chaoyang he fell ill at Yuezhou and died after one day, at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射，謚曰孝穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous title Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous title Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 子損、授、技、拭、捴，而授最賢。

translations.literal: His sons were Sun, Shou, Ji, Shi, and Zou, of whom Shou was the most worthy.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Sun, Shou, Ji, Shi, and Zou, of whom Shou was the most worthy.

sentences.zh: 授，字得符，大中九年進士擢第，釋褐從事諸侯府，入為鄠縣尉、集賢校理。

translations.literal: Shou, whose courtesy name was Defu, passed the jinshi examination in Dazhong year nine, began his career as an aide in a regional lord's secretariat, and entered court service as magistrate of Hu County and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, whose courtesy name was Defu, passed the jinshi examination in Dazhong year nine, began his career as an aide in a regional lord's secretariat, and entered court service as magistrate of Hu County and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 歷監察御史、殿中，分務東臺。

translations.literal: He served in succession as supervising censor and palace censor, with duties divided at the Eastern Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as supervising censor and palace censor, with duties divided at the Eastern Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 再遷司勛員外郎、洛陽令、兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred, becoming Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel Records, Magistrate of Luoyang, and Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted twice, becoming vice director in the Ministry of Personnel Records, magistrate of Luoyang, and vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 李福為東都留守，奏充判官，改兵部郎中，由吏部拜左諫議大夫、給事中，出為河南尹。
