translations.literal: When Li Fu was defender of the Eastern Capital, he memorialized that Shou serve as administrative aide; Shou was changed to director in the Ministry of War, then through the Ministry of Personnel was appointed Left Remonstrance Grandee and Drafting Attendant, and sent out as Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fu served as defender of the Eastern Capital, he recommended Shou as administrative aide. Shou was then made director in the Ministry of War, appointed through the Ministry of Personnel as left remonstrance grandee and drafting attendant, and sent out as intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 盧攜作相，召拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Lu Xie became chief minister, Shou was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xie became chief minister, Shou was summoned and appointed vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯京師，僖宗幸蜀，徵拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital, Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, and Shou was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao attacked the capital and Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Shou was summoned and appointed vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以母病，求散秩，改秘書監分司。

translations.literal: Because his mother was ill, he requested a nominal post and was changed to Director of the Palace Library with a commission in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was ill, he requested a nominal post and was made director of the Palace Library with a commission in the capital.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned, he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 宰相有報怨者，改左散騎常侍、國子祭酒，又轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: A chief minister who bore a grudge against him had him changed to Left Regular Attendant, Director of the Directorate of Education, and then transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister who bore a grudge against him had him reassigned as left regular attendant and director of the Directorate of Education, and then transferred him to mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 從昭宗在華下，改刑部尚書、太子少保。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Zhaozong at Hua below, he was changed to Minister of Justice and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Zhaozong at Hua below, he was made minister of justice and junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子煚，字公隱，進士及第，再遷左拾遺。

translations.literal: His son Jiong, courtesy name Gongyin, passed the jinshi examination and was twice transferred to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiong, whose courtesy name was Gongyin, passed the jinshi examination and was twice promoted to left reminder.

sentences.zh: 昭宗初即位，喜遊宴，不恤時事，煚上疏極諫，帝面賜緋袍象笏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong had just taken the throne, he delighted in feasting and touring and did not care about current affairs; Jiong submitted a memorial remonstrating forcefully, and the emperor personally granted him a crimson robe and ivory tablet.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong had just ascended the throne, he delighted in feasting and touring and paid no heed to affairs of state. Jiong submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance, and the emperor personally granted him a crimson robe and ivory tablet.

sentences.zh: 崔安潛出鎮青州，辟為支使。

translations.literal: When Cui Anqian went out to command Qingzhou, he recruited Jiong as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Anqian went out to command Qingzhou, he recruited Jiong as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 不至鎮，改太常博士。

translations.literal: He did not reach the commandery and was changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He never reached the commandery and was reassigned as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 歷主客、戶部二員外郎。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Vice Director in the Ministry of Receptions and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as vice director in the Ministry of Receptions and vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 關中亂，崔胤引硃全忠入京師，乃挈家避地湖南，官終諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When chaos erupted in Guanzhong, Cui Yin brought Zhu Quanzhong into the capital; Jiong then took his family to seek refuge in Hunan, and his final office was Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos erupted in Guanzhong and Cui Yin brought Zhu Quanzhong into the capital, Jiong took his family to seek refuge in Hunan. His final office was remonstrance grandee.

sentences.zh: 損，字子默，以廕受官，為藍田尉。

translations.literal: Sun, courtesy name Zimo, received office by inheritance and served as magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, whose courtesy name was Zimo, received office by inheritance and served as magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 三遷京兆府司錄參軍，入為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: After three transfers he became Registrar of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Jingzhao, then entered court service as palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became registrar of the metropolitan prefecture of Jingzhao, then entered court service as palace censor.

sentences.zh: 家在新昌里，與宰相路巖第相接。

translations.literal: His home was in Xinchang Ward, adjoining the residence of chief minister Lu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His home was in Xinchang Ward, adjoining the residence of chief minister Lu Yan.

sentences.zh: 巖以地狹，欲易損馬廄廣之，遣人致意。

translations.literal: Yan, finding the land narrow, wished to exchange Sun's stable to widen his own and sent someone to convey his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, finding his land too narrow, wished to swap Sun's stable to enlarge his own property and sent someone to convey the request.

sentences.zh: 時損伯叔昆仲在朝者十餘人，相與議曰：「家門損益恃時相，何可拒之？」

translations.literal: At that time more than ten of Sun's paternal uncles and brothers were at court. They discussed the matter together and said: "The rise and fall of our house depends on the chief minister of the day—how can we refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than ten of Sun's paternal uncles and brothers were at court. They discussed the matter together and said: "The rise and fall of our house depends on the chief minister of the day—how can we refuse?"

sentences.zh: 損曰：「非也。

translations.literal: Sun said: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Sun said: "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 凡尺寸地，非吾等所有。

translations.literal: Every inch of land is not ours to own.
translations.idiomatic: Every inch of land is not truly ours to dispose of.

sentences.zh: 先人舊業，安可以奉權臣？

translations.literal: Our forefathers' old property—how can it be given to serve a powerful minister?
translations.idiomatic: Our forefathers' old property—how can we give it away to serve a powerful minister?

sentences.zh: 窮達，命也。」

translations.literal: Poverty and success are a matter of fate."
translations.idiomatic: Poverty and success are a matter of fate."

sentences.zh: 巖不悅。

translations.literal: Yan was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會差制使鞫獄黔中，乃遣損使焉。

translations.literal: When a special commissioner was dispatched to investigate cases in Qianzhong, Yan sent Sun on that mission.
translations.idiomatic: When a special commissioner was dispatched to investigate cases in Qianzhong, Yan sent Sun on that mission.

sentences.zh: 逾年而還，改戶部員外郎、洛陽縣令。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned and was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Magistrate of Luoyang County.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he returned and was made vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and magistrate of Luoyang County.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部員外，出為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered court service as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and was sent out as Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and was sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 路巖罷相，徵拜給事中，遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Lu Yan was removed as chief minister, Sun was summoned and appointed Drafting Attendant and transferred to Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Yan was removed as chief minister, Sun was summoned and appointed drafting attendant and transferred to intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 盧攜作相，有宿憾，復拜給事中，出為陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: When Lu Xie became chief minister, bearing an old grudge, he had Sun again appointed Drafting Attendant and sent out as observation commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xie became chief minister, bearing an old grudge, he had Sun again appointed drafting attendant and sent out as observation commissioner of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 時軍亂，逐前使崔蕘。

translations.literal: At that time the army mutinied and drove out the previous commissioner Cui Rao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the army mutinied and drove out the previous commissioner Cui Rao.

sentences.zh: 損至，盡誅其亂首。

translations.literal: When Sun arrived, he executed all the ringleaders of the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun arrived, he executed all the ringleaders of the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 逾年，改青州刺史、御史大夫、淄青節度使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was changed to Prefect of Qingzhou, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Governor of the Ziqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made prefect of Qingzhou, censor-in-chief, and military governor of the Ziqing circuit.

sentences.zh: 又檢校刑部尚書、鄆州刺史、天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was further made acting Minister of Justice, prefect of Yunzhou, and military governor of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made acting Minister of Justice, prefect of Yunzhou, and military governor of the Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 未赴鄆，復留青州，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: Before he could go to Yan, he was again kept at Qingzhou and died in his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could go to Yan, he was again kept at Qingzhou and died in his commandery.

sentences.zh: 技進士及第，位至中書舍人。

translations.literal: Ji passed the jinshi examination and rose to Drafting Secretary at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji passed the jinshi examination and rose to drafting secretary at the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 拭官終考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Shi's final office was Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's final office was vice director in the Ministry of Personnel Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 捴終兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Zou ended as Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Zou ended his career as director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 拭、捴並進士擢第。

translations.literal: Shi and Zou both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Zou both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 楊虞卿，字師臯，虢州弘農人。

translations.literal: Yang Yuqing, courtesy name Shigao, was a native of Hongnong in Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuqing, whose courtesy name was Shigao, was a native of Hongnong in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖燕客。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Yanke.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Yanke.

sentences.zh: 父寧，貞元中為長安尉。

translations.literal: His father Ning served as magistrate of Chang'an during the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning served as magistrate of Chang'an during the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 少有棲遁之志，以處士徵入朝。

translations.literal: From youth he had a wish to live in reclusion and was summoned to court as a retired scholar.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he wished to live in reclusion and was summoned to court as a retired scholar.

sentences.zh: 有口辯，優遊公卿間。

translations.literal: He had a gift for debate and moved at ease among dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for debate and moved at ease among dukes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 竇參尤重之，會參貶，仕進不達而卒。

translations.literal: Dou Can especially valued him; when Can was demoted, he did not advance in office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can especially valued him, but when Can was demoted he did not advance in office and died.

sentences.zh: 虞卿，元和五年進士擢第，又應博學宏辭科。

translations.literal: Yuqing passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year five and also passed the Broad Learning and Eloquent Discourse examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year five and also passed the Broad Learning and Eloquent Discourse examination.

sentences.zh: 元和末，累官至監察御史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era, he rose in succession to supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe era, he rose in succession to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初即位，不修政道，盤遊無節，虞卿上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong had just taken the throne, he did not cultivate the way of government and indulged in roaming and feasting without restraint; Yuqing submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong had just ascended the throne, he neglected the way of government and indulged in roaming and feasting without restraint. Yuqing submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞鳶烏遭害則仁鳥逝，誹謗不誅則良言進。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that when the kite and crow meet harm, the benevolent birds depart; when slander is not punished, good counsel advances.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when the kite and crow meet harm, the benevolent birds depart, and that when slander goes unpunished, good counsel advances.

sentences.zh: 況詔旨勉諭，許陳愚誠，故臣不敢避誅，以獻狂瞽。

translations.literal: Moreover an edict encouraged and instructed, permitting the stating of sincere but foolish views; therefore your subject dares not avoid punishment and offers this reckless blindness.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty's edict encouraged frank counsel and permitted the stating of sincere but foolish views, so I dare not hold back for fear of punishment and offer this reckless blindness.

sentences.zh: 竊聞堯、舜受命，以天下為憂，不聞以位為樂。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately heard that when Yao and Shun received the mandate, they took the realm as their worry and did not hear of taking the throne as their pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Yao and Shun received the mandate, they took the realm as their worry and did not treat the throne as a source of pleasure.

sentences.zh: 況北虜猶梗，西戎未賓，兩河之瘡磐未平，五嶺之妖氛未解。

translations.literal: Moreover the northern barbarians still block the way, the western Rong have not submitted, the wounds of the Two He Rivers are not yet healed, and the demonic miasma of the Five Ridges is not yet dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the northern barbarians still obstruct the frontier, the western Rong have not submitted, the wounds of the Two He Rivers are not yet healed, and the demonic miasma of the Five Ridges is not yet dispelled.

sentences.zh: 生人之疾苦盡在，朝廷之制度莫修，邊儲屢空，國用猶屈。

translations.literal: The suffering of the living is all present, the court's institutions are not repaired, frontier stores are repeatedly empty, and state revenue is still strained.
translations.idiomatic: The suffering of the people is everywhere present, the court's institutions go unrepaired, frontier stores are repeatedly empty, and state revenue is still strained.

sentences.zh: 固未可以高枕無虞也。

translations.literal: Surely one cannot yet pillow one's head high without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Surely one cannot yet rest easy without worry.

sentences.zh: 陛下初臨萬宇，有憂天下之志。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has just come to rule the myriad realms and has the will to worry for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has just come to rule the realm and has shown the will to worry for the world.

sentences.zh: 宜日延輔臣公卿百執事，凝旒而問，造膝以求，使四方內外，有所觀焉。

translations.literal: One ought daily to extend audience to chief ministers, dukes and lords, and the hundred officials, sitting with lowered tassels to inquire and drawing near to seek counsel, so that within and without, all quarters have something to observe.
translations.idiomatic: You ought daily to receive chief ministers, dukes and lords, and the hundred officials, sitting attentively to inquire and drawing them near to seek counsel, so that all within and without the realm have something to observe.

sentences.zh: 自聽政已來，六十日矣，八開延英，獨三數大臣仰龍顏，承聖問。

translations.literal: Since assuming governance, sixty days have passed; Yanying has been opened eight times, yet only a few chief ministers looked up at the dragon countenance and received imperial inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Since you began to govern, sixty days have passed. Yanying has been opened eight times, yet only a few chief ministers have looked up at your countenance and received your questions.

sentences.zh: 其餘侍從詔誥之臣，偕入而齊出，何足以聞政事哉！

translations.literal: The rest of the attendant edict-drafting officials entered together and left together—how could that suffice to hear affairs of government!
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the attendant edict-drafting officials entered together and left together. How could that suffice to hear affairs of government!

sentences.zh: 諫臣盈廷，忠言未聞於聖聽，臣實羞之。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials fill the court, yet loyal words are not heard by the holy ear—your subject is truly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials fill the court, yet loyal words are not heard by Your Majesty. I am truly ashamed.

sentences.zh: 蓋由主恩尚疏，而眾正之路未啟也。

translations.literal: This is because sovereign favor is still distant, and the path for the upright multitude has not yet been opened.
translations.idiomatic: This is because Your Majesty's favor is still distant, and the path for upright officials has not yet been opened.

sentences.zh: 夫公卿大臣，宜朝夕接見論道，賜與從容，則君臣之情相接，而理道備聞矣。

translations.literal: Chief ministers and great officials ought to be received morning and evening to discuss the Way, granted leisurely audience—then the sentiments of ruler and minister would connect, and the principles of governance would be fully heard.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers and great officials ought to be received morning and evening to discuss the Way and granted leisurely audience. Then the bond between ruler and minister would be joined, and the principles of governance would be fully heard.

sentences.zh: 今自宰相已下四五人，時得頃刻侍坐，天威不遠，鞠躬隕越，隨旨上下，無能往來。

translations.literal: Now from the chief minister down, only four or five men at times receive a moment's audience; the heavenly awe is not far—they bow with trembling, rising and falling with the imperial will, unable to engage in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Now from the chief minister down, only four or five men at times receive a moment's audience. Your Majesty's awe is close at hand—they bow in trembling submission, rising and falling with your will, unable to engage in real exchange.

sentences.zh: 此由君太尊、臣太卑故也。

translations.literal: This is because the ruler is too lofty and the ministers too humble.
translations.idiomatic: This is because Your Majesty stands too far above them and your ministers bow too low.

sentences.zh: 自公卿已下，雖歷踐清地，曾未祗奉天睠，以承下問，郁塞正路，偷安幸門。

translations.literal: From the chief ministers down, though they have trodden pure stations, they have never reverently received heaven's favor to accept inquiry from below—they block the right path and steal ease at the gate of good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: From the chief ministers down, though they have risen through honorable offices, none has reverently received Your Majesty's favor to answer your questions. They clog the path of upright counsel and seek comfort through flattery and favor.

sentences.zh: 況陛下神聖如五帝，臣下莫能望清光。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty is as sacred as the Five Emperors; subordinates cannot gaze upon your clear radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty is as sacred as the Five Emperors, and your officials cannot even approach the radiance of your presence.

sentences.zh: 所宜周遍顧問，惠其氣色，使支體相輔，君臣喻明。

translations.literal: What is fitting is to inquire comprehensively everywhere, bestow favor upon their countenance, cause limbs and trunk to assist each other, and make ruler and minister mutually clear in understanding.
translations.idiomatic: You ought to inquire broadly of all, grant them the warmth of your attention, so that the whole body of government works in concert and ruler and ministers understand one another clearly.

sentences.zh: 陛下求理於公卿，公卿求理於臣輩，自然上下孜孜相問，使進忠若趨利，論政若訴冤。

translations.literal: Your Majesty seeking governance from chief ministers, chief ministers seeking governance from our kind—naturally above and below would diligently inquire of each other, making the offering of loyalty like rushing toward profit and discussing government like pleading a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty seeks good governance from the chief ministers, and the chief ministers seek it from the ranks below, naturally all levels would earnestly question one another—offering loyal counsel as eagerly as pursuing profit, and debating policy as urgently as pleading a grievance.

sentences.zh: 如此而不聞過失、不致升平者，未之有也。

translations.literal: Acting thus yet not hearing of faults and not attaining great peace—there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: If this were done and you still failed to hear of your errors or bring the realm to great peace, there would be no precedent for it.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王，居危思安之心不相殊，而居安慮危之心不相及，故不得皆為聖帝明王。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, emperors and kings—the mind that in peril thinks of safety is not different, but the mind that in safety considers peril does not reach the same level; therefore not all could become sage emperors and enlightened kings.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, all emperors and kings alike think of safety when in peril, but few think of peril when at ease. That is why not all could become sage emperors and enlightened kings.

sentences.zh: 小臣疏賤，豈宜及此，獨不忍冒榮偷祿，以負聖朝。

translations.literal: This petty official is remote and lowly—how should I speak to this? I alone cannot bear to accept glory and steal salary, thereby failing the sacred court.
translations.idiomatic: I am a lowly and insignificant official—what business have I speaking of such things? I alone cannot bear to enjoy rank and salary without speaking the truth, and thereby fail the sacred court.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty consider it.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider this.

sentences.zh: 帝深獎其言。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor highly praised his memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋令奉使西北邊，犒賞戍卒，遷侍御史，再轉禮部員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered on mission to the northwest border to reward border garrison troops; he was promoted to attendant censor, then transferred again to vice director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was sent on mission to the northwest frontier to reward the garrison troops. He was promoted to attendant censor, then again to vice director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年八月，改吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Changqing year four, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Changqing year four, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，南曹令史李幹等六人，偽出告身簽符，賣鑿空偽官，令赴任者六十五人，取受錢一萬六千七百三十貫。

translations.literal: In Taihe year two, six clerks of the Southern Bureau, including Li Gan, forged appointment commissions and signature seals, sold fabricated government posts to sixty-five men who took up their assignments, and accepted bribes totaling sixteen thousand seven hundred thirty strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year two, six clerks of the Southern Bureau, including Li Gan, forged appointment commissions and signature seals, sold fabricated government posts to sixty-five men who took up their assignments, and accepted bribes totaling sixteen thousand seven hundred thirty strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 虞卿按得偽狀，捕幹等移御史臺鞫劾。

translations.literal: Yuqing, having investigated and obtained proof of the forgery, arrested Gan and the others and transferred them to the Censorate for interrogation and impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing investigated the case, obtained proof of the forgery, arrested Gan and the others, and handed them over to the Censorate for trial.

sentences.zh: 幹稱六人共率錢二千貫，與虞卿廳典溫亮，求不發舉偽濫事跡。

translations.literal: Gan stated that the six men together raised two thousand strings of cash and gave them to Yuqing's bureau chief Wen Liang, seeking that the matter of forged and abusive appointments not be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Gan testified that the six of them had pooled two thousand strings of cash and paid Yuqing's bureau administrator Wen Liang to keep the matter of forged appointments from being reported.

sentences.zh: 乃詔給事中嚴休復、中書舍人高鉞、左丞韋景休充三司推案，而溫亮逃竄。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict appointed Supervising Secretary Yan Xiufu, Secretariat Drafter Gao Yue, and Left Vice Director Wei Jingxiu to serve as the three-department investigation team, while Wen Liang fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Supervising Secretary Yan Xiufu, Secretariat Drafter Gao Yue, and Left Vice Director Wei Jingxiu to conduct a three-department investigation, while Wen Liang fled.

sentences.zh: 幹等既伏誅，虞卿以檢下無術，停見任。

translations.literal: After Gan and the others had been executed, Yuqing, for lacking skill in supervising subordinates, was suspended from his current post.
translations.idiomatic: After Gan and the others were executed, Yuqing was suspended from office for his failure to supervise his subordinates properly.

sentences.zh: 及李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政，起為左司郎中。

translations.literal: When Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru served as chief ministers, he was recalled as director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru came to power, he was recalled and appointed director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，拜諫議大夫，充弘文館學士，判院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, he was appointed remonstrance adviser, made a scholar of the Hongwen Pavilion, and assigned to administer its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year, he was appointed remonstrance adviser, made a scholar of the Hongwen Pavilion, and put in charge of its administration.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉給事中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was transferred to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 七年，宗閔罷相，李德裕知政事，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Zongmin was dismissed as chief minister; Li Deyu took charge of government affairs, and Yuqing was sent out as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Zongmin was dismissed as chief minister and Li Deyu took charge of government affairs. Yuqing was sent out as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 虞卿性柔佞，能阿附權幸以為奸利。

translations.literal: Yuqing's nature was soft and flattering; he could fawn upon the powerful and favored to seek wicked profit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing was soft-spoken and sycophantic, skilled at currying favor with the powerful for illicit gain.

sentences.zh: 每歲銓曹貢部，為舉選人馳走取科第，占員闕，無不得其所欲；

translations.literal: Every year, in the selection bureaus and the examination department, he ran about for examination candidates to obtain degrees and secure vacant posts—there was nothing they did not get as they wished;
translations.idiomatic: Every year at examination season he pulled strings for candidates at the selection and examination bureaus—winning degrees, securing vacant posts—nothing they wanted was beyond his reach;

sentences.zh: 升沈取舍，出其脣吻。

translations.literal: Advancement, demotion, acceptance, and rejection came from his lips.
translations.idiomatic: Who rose, who fell, who was accepted and who was rejected—all depended on his word.

sentences.zh: 而李宗閔待之如骨肉，以能朋比唱和，故時號黨魁。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin treated him like bone and flesh; because he could form factions and sing in chorus, he was at the time called the faction leader.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin treated him like family, and because he excelled at building factional alliances, he was known at the time as the ringleader of the clique.

sentences.zh: 八年，宗閔復入相，尋召為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Zongmin again entered the chief ministership; soon Yuqing was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Zongmin returned as chief minister, and Yuqing was soon recalled as vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year, he was appointed metropolitan governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year, he was appointed metropolitan governor of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，京師訛言鄭註為上合金丹，須小兒心肝，密旨捕小兒無算。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, a rumor spread in the capital that Zheng Zhu, to compound an elixir of immortality for the emperor, required children's heart and liver; by secret edict, children were seized without number.
translations.idiomatic: That same June, a rumor spread through the capital that Zheng Zhu was compounding an elixir of immortality for the emperor and needed children's hearts and livers—and on secret orders, countless children were seized.

sentences.zh: 民間相告語，扃鎖小兒甚密，街肆洶洶。

translations.literal: Among the people they told one another; children were locked away with great tightness; the streets and markets were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: People warned one another, locked their children indoors, and the streets and markets erupted in panic.

sentences.zh: 上聞之不悅，鄭註頗不自安。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was displeased; Zheng Zhu was rather ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he was displeased, and Zheng Zhu grew deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李固言素嫉虞卿朋黨，乃奏曰：「臣昨窮問其由，此語出於京兆尹從人，因此扇於都下。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Guyen, who had long resented Yuqing's faction, memorialized: "When I thoroughly investigated the matter yesterday, I found that this talk originated with the metropolitan governor's attendants and was spread throughout the capital from there."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Guyen, who had long resented Yuqing's faction, memorialized: "When I thoroughly investigated the matter yesterday, I found that this talk originated with the metropolitan governor's attendants and was spread throughout the capital from there."

sentences.zh: 上怒，即令收虞卿下獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and immediately ordered Yuqing seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and immediately ordered Yuqing arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 虞卿弟漢公並男知進等八人自系，撾鼓訴冤，詔虞卿歸私第。

translations.literal: Yuqing's younger brother Hangong together with his sons Zhijin and seven others bound themselves, beat the drum to plead grievance, and an edict ordered Yuqing to return to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's younger brother Hangong and his son Zhijin together with six others bound themselves and beat the grievance drum. The emperor then ordered Yuqing released to his home.

sentences.zh: 翌日，貶虔州司馬，再貶虔州司戶，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: The next day, he was demoted to military adjutant of Qian Prefecture; demoted again to registrar of Qian Prefecture; he died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was demoted to military adjutant of Qian Prefecture, then demoted again to registrar of the same prefecture, and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 子知進、知退、堪，弟漢公，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Zhijin, Zhuitui, and Kan, and his younger brother Hangong—all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhijin, Zhuitui, and Kan, and his younger brother Hangong, all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 知退歷都官、戶部二郎中；

translations.literal: Zhuitui served as director of both the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuitui served as director in both the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 堪庫部、吏部二員外郎。

translations.literal: Kan served as vice director in both the Ministry of Revenue and the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Kan served as vice director in both the Ministry of Revenue and the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 漢公，太和八年擢進士第，又書判拔萃，釋褐為李絳興元從事。

translations.literal: Hangong passed the jinshi examination in Taihe year eight, also excelled in the written judgment examination, and upon entering office became a staff member under Li Jiang in Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hangong passed the jinshi examination in Taihe year eight, also excelled in the written judgment examination, and upon entering office became a staff member under Li Jiang in Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 絳遇害，漢公遁而獲免。

translations.literal: When Jiang was murdered, Hangong fled and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiang was murdered, Hangong fled and escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部郎中、史館修撰，

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the Ministry of Revenue and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several promotions to director of the Ministry of Revenue and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 太和七年，遷司封郎中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe, He was transferred to director of the Department of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taihe, He was then transferred to director of the Department of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 漢公子範、籌，皆登進士第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: Hangong's sons Fan and Chou both passed the jinshi examination and were repeatedly recruited to military commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Hangong's sons Fan and Chou both passed the jinshi examination and were repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 虞卿從兄汝士。

translations.literal: Yuqing's elder cousin was Rushi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's elder cousin was Rushi.

sentences.zh: 汝士，字慕巢，元和四年進士擢第，又登博學宏詞科，累辟使府。

translations.literal: Rushi, whose courtesy name was Muchao, passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year four, also passed the Erudite and Literary examination, and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi, whose courtesy name was Muchao, passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year four, also passed the Erudite and Literary examination, and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年為右補闕。

translations.literal: In Changqing year one he became Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing year one he became Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 坐弟殷士貢舉覆落，貶開江令。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Yinshi failed the reread of the examination results, he was demoted to magistrate of Kaijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Because his younger brother Yinshi was struck from the examination rolls upon rereading, Rushi was demoted to magistrate of Kaijiang.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部員外，再遷職方郎中。

translations.literal: He entered service as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, and was again transferred to director of the Bureau of Posts and Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, then promoted again to director of the Bureau of Posts and Carriages.

sentences.zh: 太和三年七月，以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, in the seventh month, with his existing rank he was made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe, in the seventh month, he was made drafter of edicts while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 時李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政，待汝士厚。

translations.literal: At the time Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru held chief ministerships and treated Rushi generously.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru were chief ministers and treated Rushi with great favor.

sentences.zh: 尋正拜中書舍人，改工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was formally appointed secretariat drafter and transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon formally appointed secretariat drafter and transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 八年，出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was sent out as prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, he was sent out as prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九年九月，入為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year, he entered service as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the ninth year, he was recalled as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 開成元年七月，轉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng, in the seventh month, he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaicheng, in the seventh month, he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: That December he was made acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military governor of Jiannan East-Chuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That December he was made acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military governor of Jiannan East-Chuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時宗人嗣復鎮西川，兄弟對居節制，時人榮之。

translations.literal: At the time his clansman Sifu governed Western Chuan; the brothers both held military commissionerships—a thing people at the time regarded with honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his clansman Sifu governed Western Chuan, and the two brothers held neighboring military commissions—a distinction people greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，入為吏部侍郎，位至尚書，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year, he entered service as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, rose to minister, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year he was recalled as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, rose to minister, and died.

sentences.zh: 子知溫、知遠、知權，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Zhiwen, Zhiyuan, and Zhiquan all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhiwen, Zhiyuan, and Zhiquan all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 汝士子 知溫知溫累官至禮部郎中、知制誥，入為翰林學士、戶部侍郎，轉左丞。

translations.literal: Rushi's son Zhiwen—Zhiwen rose through many offices to director of the Ministry of Rites and drafter of edicts, entered service as Hanlin academician and vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, and was transferred to left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi's son Zhiwen rose through the ranks to director of the Ministry of Rites and drafter of edicts, then became a Hanlin academician and vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, and was promoted to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為河南尹、陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as governor of Henan and observation commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Henan and observation commissioner of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校兵部尚書、襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting Minister of War, prefect of Xiangzhou, and military commissioner of Shannandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Minister of War, prefect of Xiangzhou, and military commissioner of Shannandong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 知溫弟 知至知溫弟知至，累官至比部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Zhiwen's younger brother Zhizhi—Zhiwen's younger brother Zhizhi—rose through many offices to director of the Bureau of Review and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen's younger brother Zhizhi rose through the ranks to director of the Bureau of Review and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 坐故府劉瞻罷相，貶官。

translations.literal: Because his former superior Liu Zhan was dismissed as chief minister, he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When his former superior Liu Zhan was dismissed as chief minister, Zhizhi was demoted.

sentences.zh: 知至亦貶瓊州司馬。

translations.literal: Zhizhi was also demoted to military adjutant of Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi was also demoted to military adjutant of Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為諫議大夫，累遷京兆尹、工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered service as remonstrance adviser, and was repeatedly promoted to metropolitan governor and vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as remonstrance adviser and rose through several promotions to metropolitan governor and vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 知溫、知至皆位至列曹尚書。

translations.literal: Zhiwen and Zhizhi both reached the rank of ministers of their respective bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zhiwen and Zhizhi rose to the rank of bureau minister.

sentences.zh: 汝士弟 魯士汝士弟魯士。

translations.literal: Rushi's younger brother Lushi, Rushi's younger brother Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi's younger brother Lushi.

sentences.zh: 魯士，字宗尹，本名殷士，

translations.literal: Lushi, courtesy name Zongyin, original name Yinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Lushi, whose courtesy name was Zongyin, was originally named Yinshi.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，進士擢第，其年詔翰林覆試。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, He passed the jinshi examination; that year an edict ordered a reread by the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing, He passed the jinshi examination, and that year the Hanlin Academy was ordered to reread the results.

sentences.zh: 殷士與鄭朗等覆落，因改名魯士。

translations.literal: Yinshi together with Zheng Lang and others failed the reread; therefore he changed his name to Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshi, along with Zheng Lang and others, was struck from the rolls upon rereading, and he therefore changed his name to Lushi.

sentences.zh: 復登制科，位不達而卒。

translations.literal: He again passed the decree examination, but his rank did not attain high office before he died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the decree examination as well, but never rose high before he died.

sentences.zh: 初汝士中第，有時名，遂歷清貫。

translations.literal: At first when Rushi passed the examination he had a reputation of the age and thereafter went through pure sinecures.
translations.idiomatic: When Rushi first passed the examination he was widely known and went on to serve in prestigious central offices.

sentences.zh: 其年諸子皆至正卿，郁為昌族。

translations.literal: Within years all his sons reached chief ministers; they flourished as a prosperous clan.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years all his sons reached the highest ministerial ranks, and the clan flourished in prominence.

sentences.zh: 所居靜恭里，知溫兄弟，並列門戟。

translations.literal: At their residence in Jinggong Lane, the Zhiwen brothers all displayed gate halberds side by side.
translations.idiomatic: At their residence in Jinggong Lane, the Zhiwen brothers all displayed their gate halberds side by side—a mark of high official rank.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，昆仲子孫，在朝行方鎮者十餘人。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong era, among the brothers and their descendants, more than ten served in the court ranks or as regional commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era, more than ten members of the clan and their descendants held office at court or as regional commissioners.

sentences.zh: 馬植，扶風人。

translations.literal: Ma Zhi, Ma Zhi, a native of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi was a native of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父曛。

translations.literal: His father was Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Xun.

sentences.zh: 植，元和十四年進士擢第，又登制策科，釋褐壽州團練副使。

translations.literal: Zhi passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year fourteen, also passed the decree policy examination, and upon entering office became deputy regimental trainer of Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year fourteen, also passed the decree policy examination, and upon entering office became deputy regimental trainer of Shou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 得秘書省校書郎，三遷饒州刺史。

translations.literal: He obtained the post of collator in the Secretariat; after three promotions he became prefect of Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed collator in the Secretariat and after three promotions became prefect of Rao.

sentences.zh: 開成初，遷安南都護、御史中丞、安南招討使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, he was transferred to protector-general of Annam, vice censor-in-chief, and pacification commissioner of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, he was appointed protector-general of Annam, vice censor-in-chief, and pacification commissioner of Annam.

sentences.zh: 植文雅之餘，長於吏術。

translations.literal: Beyond literary refinement, Zhi excelled at the arts of administration.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond his literary refinement, Zhi excelled at practical administration.

sentences.zh: 三年，奏：「當管羈縻州首領，或居巢穴自固，或為南蠻所誘，不可招諭，事有可虞。

translations.literal: In the third year, he memorialized: "The chieftains of the attached prefectures under my jurisdiction—some dwell in mountain lairs and hold themselves secure, some are enticed by the southern barbarians—cannot be summoned and persuaded; the matter gives cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he memorialized: "The chieftains of the attached prefectures under my jurisdiction either hide in mountain strongholds or are lured by the southern tribes. They cannot be won by persuasion alone, and the situation is worrisome.

sentences.zh: 臣自到鎮，約之以信誠，曉之以逆順。

translations.literal: Since Your subject arrived at my post, I have bound them with faith and sincerity and instructed them in what is rebellious and what is compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Since I arrived at my post, I have treated them with sincerity and explained to them the difference between rebellion and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今諸首領，總發忠言，願納賦稅。

translations.literal: Now all the chieftains have altogether spoken loyal words and wish to deliver taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Now all the chieftains have pledged their loyalty and expressed willingness to pay tribute and taxes.

sentences.zh: 其武陸縣請升為州，以首領為刺史。」

translations.literal: I request that Wulu County be elevated to prefectural status, with the chieftain appointed as prefect."
translations.idiomatic: I request that Wulu County be elevated to prefectural status, with the chieftain appointed as prefect."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又奏陸州界廢珠池復生珠。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that within the borders of Lu Prefecture an abandoned pearl pool had again produced pearls.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that an abandoned pearl pool within Lu Prefecture had begun producing pearls again.

sentences.zh: 以能政，就加檢校左散騎常侍，加中散大夫，轉黔中觀察使。

translations.literal: For able governance, he was further granted acting left regular attendant-at-large, promoted to grand master of palace attendance, and transferred to observation commissioner of Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: For his capable administration he was further granted acting left regular attendant-at-large and promoted to grand master of palace attendance, then transferred to observation commissioner of Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，入為大理卿。

translations.literal: During the Huichang era, he entered service as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang era, he was recalled as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 植以文學政事為時所知。

translations.literal: Zhi was known to his age for literature, learning, and political affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was known to his contemporaries for both literary talent and administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 久在邊遠，及還朝，不獲顯官，必微有望，李德裕素不重之。

translations.literal: Long stationed on distant frontiers, when he returned to court he did not obtain a prominent post—his hopes were slight; Li Deyu had never valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: After long service on distant frontiers, he returned to court without receiving a prominent post, nursed private hopes of advancement, and Li Deyu had never held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，宰相白敏中與德裕有隙，凡德裕所薄者，必不次拔擢之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Chief Minister Bai Minzhong had a rift with Deyu; all whom Deyu looked down upon were invariably promoted out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, Chief Minister Bai Minzhong, who was at odds with Deyu, invariably promoted out of turn everyone Deyu had looked down upon.

sentences.zh: 乃加植金紫光祿大夫，行刑部侍郎，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhi was granted the golden purple light grand master of the palace, acting vice director of the Ministry of Justice, and commissioner of salt and iron transport for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was then granted the golden purple light grand master of the palace, appointed acting vice director of the Ministry of Justice, and made commissioner of salt and iron transport for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 轉戶部侍郎，領使如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, continuing as commissioner as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue while retaining his commissionership.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官同平章事，遷中書侍郎，兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon with his existing rank he became co-chief minister of the Secretariat, was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, and concurrently minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made co-chief minister of the Secretariat with his existing rank, promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, and concurrently minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 敏中罷相，植亦罷為太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: When Minzhong was dismissed as chief minister, Zhi was also dismissed as guest of the heir apparent and assigned to the eastern capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: When Minzhong left office, Zhi was also dismissed and made guest of the heir apparent with duties at the eastern capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 數年，出為許州刺史、檢校刑部尚書、忠武軍節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: After several years, he was sent out as prefect of Xu Prefecture, acting minister of justice, and military commissioner and observation commissioner of the Zhongwu Army and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was sent out as prefect of Xu, acting minister of justice, and military and observation commissioner of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 大中末，遷汴州刺史、宣武軍節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dazhong era, he was transferred to prefect of Bian Prefecture and military commissioner and observation commissioner of the Xuanwu Army and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Dazhong era, he was transferred to prefect of Bian and military and observation commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮。

translations.literal: He died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving in that post.

sentences.zh: 李讓夷，字達心，隴西人。

translations.literal: Li Rangyi, Li Rangyi, courtesy name Daxin, a native of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rangyi, whose courtesy name was Daxin, was a native of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 祖悅，父應規。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Yue; his father was Yinggui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Yue and his father was Yinggui.

sentences.zh: 讓夷，元和十四年擢進士第，釋褐諸侯府。

translations.literal: Rangyi passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year fourteen and began his career in a regional lord's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Rangyi passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year fourteen and began his career in a regional lord's staff.

sentences.zh: 太和初入朝，為右拾遺，召充翰林學士，轉左補闕。

translations.literal: In the early Taihe era he entered court, served as Right Reminder, was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician, and was transferred to Left Supplementation Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign he entered court as Right Reminder, was appointed Hanlin Academician, and was then transferred to Left Supplementation Aide.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷職方員外郎、左司郎中，充職。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments and Left Department Director and filled both posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments and Left Department Director, serving in both capacities.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜諫議大夫，

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Remonstrance and Policy Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Remonstrance and Policy Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，以本官兼知起居舍人事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng, With his existing office he concurrently served as acting Diarist of Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaicheng, He also concurrently served as acting Diarist of Imperial Audience while retaining his existing post.

sentences.zh: 時起居舍人李褒有痼疾，請罷官。

translations.literal: At that time the Diarist Li Bao had a chronic illness and requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Diarist Li Bao suffered from a chronic illness and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 宰臣李石奏闕官，上曰：「褚遂良為諫議大夫，嘗兼此官，卿可盡言今諫議大夫姓名。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Shi reported the vacancy. The emperor said, "Chu Suiliang served as Remonstrance and Policy Grand Master and once held this post concurrently. State the full names of the current Remonstrance and Policy Grandees."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Shi reported the vacancy. The emperor said, "Chu Suiliang served as Remonstrance and Policy Grand Master and once held this post concurrently. State the full names of the current Remonstrance and Policy Grandees."

sentences.zh: 石遂奏李讓夷、馮定、孫簡、蕭俶。

translations.literal: Li Shi then memorialized Li Rangyi, Feng Ding, Sun Jian, and Xiao Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi then named Li Rangyi, Feng Ding, Sun Jian, and Xiao Chu.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「讓夷可也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Rangyi will do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Rangyi will do."

sentences.zh: 李固言欲用崔球、張次宗。

translations.literal: Li Guyuan wanted to use Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guyuan wanted to appoint Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「崔球遊宗閔之門，赤墀下秉筆記註，為千古法，不可用朋黨。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "Cui Qiu frequents Li Zongmin's faction. Below the red steps, holding the brush to record and annotate is the law for a thousand ages. One must not use factional partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "Cui Qiu moves in Li Zongmin's circle. Recording and annotating below the red steps is a precedent for all time. Factional favorites must not be used.

sentences.zh: 如裴中孺、李讓夷，臣不敢有纖芥異論。」

translations.literal: As for Pei Zhongru and Li Rangyi, I have not the slightest objection."
translations.idiomatic: As for Pei Zhongru and Li Rangyi, I have not the slightest objection."

sentences.zh: 其為人主大臣知重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which sovereign and chief ministers held him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which the emperor and his chief ministers held him.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Palace Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Palace Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 以鄭覃此言，深為李玨、楊嗣復所惡，終文宗世，官不達。

translations.literal: Because of this remark by Zheng Tan, he was deeply hated by Li Jue and Yang Sifu, and through the entire reign of Emperor Wenzong his office did not reach high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Zheng Tan's remark, he was deeply resented by Li Jue and Yang Sifu, and throughout Emperor Wenzong's reign he never rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 及德裕秉政，驟加拔擢，歷工、戶二侍郎，轉左丞。

translations.literal: When De Yu took power, he was suddenly raised and promoted, serving successively as Vice Ministers of Works and Revenue, then transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu came to power, he was suddenly promoted, serving in turn as Vice Minister of Works and Vice Minister of Revenue before becoming Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校尚書右僕射，俄拜中書侍郎，同平章事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Associate Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon became Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Councilor.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位罷相，以太子賓客分司卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded he was removed as councilor, served as Crown Prince Guest of Honor in a branch office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne he was dismissed as councilor, served as Crown Prince Guest of Honor in a branch post, and died there.

sentences.zh: 魏謩，字申之，鉅鹿人。

translations.literal: Wei Mo, styled Shenzhi, was a man of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mo, styled Shenzhi, was a native of Julu.

sentences.zh: 五代祖文貞公徵，貞觀朝名相。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Duke Wen Zhen Wei Zheng was a renowned chancellor in the Zhenguan reign.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor, Duke Wen Zhen Wei Zheng, was a famous chancellor of the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 曾祖殷，汝陽令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yin was magistrate of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yin served as magistrate of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 祖明，亦為縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ming also served as a county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ming also served as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 父馮，獻陵臺令。

translations.literal: His father Feng was director of the Xian Mausoleum Platform.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feng was director of the Xian Mausoleum Platform.

sentences.zh: 謩，太和七年登進士第。

translations.literal: Mo passed the jinshi examination in Taihe year seven.
translations.idiomatic: Mo passed the jinshi examination in Taihe year seven.

sentences.zh: 楊汝士牧同州，辟為防禦判官，得秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: When Yang Rushi governed Tong prefecture, he recruited him as defense staff judge, and he obtained the post of Collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Rushi was prefect of Tongzhou, he recruited Mo as defense staff judge, and Mo received appointment as Collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 汝士入朝，薦為右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Rushi entered court, he recommended him as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Rushi entered court, he recommended Mo for the post of Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 文宗以謩魏徵之裔，頗奇待之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, because Mo was a descendant of Wei Zheng, treated him with considerable favor and distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mo was a descendant of Wei Zheng, Emperor Wenzong treated him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 前邕管經略使董昌齡枉殺錄事參軍衡方厚，坐貶漵州司戶。

translations.literal: Former Yongguan Military Commissioner Dong Changling had wrongly killed recording secretary Heng Fanghou; for this he was demoted to Registrar of Xu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The former Yongguan Military Commissioner Dong Changling had unjustly killed recording secretary Heng Fanghou and was demoted to registrar of Xu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至是量移硤州刺史，謩上疏論之曰：「王者施渙汗之恩以赦有罪，唯故意殺人無赦。

translations.literal: At this time he was transferred by equivalency to prefect of Xia prefecture. Mo submitted a memorial arguing: "A king bestows the grace of sweeping benevolence to pardon the guilty; only deliberate murder knows no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he was transferred by equivalency to prefect of Xiazhou. Mo submitted a memorial arguing, "A ruler extends sweeping mercy to pardon the guilty, but deliberate murder is never pardoned.

sentences.zh: 昌齡比者錄以微效，授之方隅，不能祗慎寵光，恣其狂暴，無辜專殺，事跡顯彰。

translations.literal: Changling recently was recorded for slight merit and granted a border post; he could not reverently respect the honor shown him, indulged his brutality, wantonly killed the innocent — the facts are conspicuously clear.
translations.idiomatic: Changling was recently noted for minor service and given a frontier post, yet he failed to honor the favor shown him, gave free rein to his violence, and murdered an innocent man — the facts are plain.

sentences.zh: 妻孥銜冤，萬里披訴。

translations.literal: His wife and children bore grievance and traveled ten thousand li to lay their petition.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children nursed their grievance and traveled a thousand miles to plead their case.

sentences.zh: 及按鞫伏罪，貸以微生，中外議論，以為屈法。

translations.literal: When investigation established his guilt, he was spared with a light sentence; inside and outside the court there was talk that the law had been bent.
translations.idiomatic: When investigation proved his guilt, he was spared with a light sentence, and opinion inside and outside the court held that the law had been bent.

sentences.zh: 今若授之牧守，以理疲人，則殺人者拔擢，而冤苦者何伸？

translations.literal: If he is now granted a prefecture to govern the weary people, then the killer is promoted — how can the wronged be redressed?
translations.idiomatic: If he is now made a prefect to govern the people, a killer is promoted while the wronged have no redress — how can that be justified?

sentences.zh: 交紊憲章，有乘至理。」

translations.literal: This would overturn the law and violate fundamental principle."
translations.idiomatic: This would overturn the law and violate fundamental principle."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，乃改為洪州別駕。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the appointment was changed to Vice Prefect of Hong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the appointment was changed to Vice Prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞李孝本，皇族也，坐李訓誅，有女沒人掖廷。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Xiaoben, of the imperial clan, was implicated in Li Xun's execution; his daughter was taken into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Xiaoben, a member of the imperial clan, was implicated in Li Xun's purge, and his daughter was taken into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 謩諫曰：

translations.literal: Mo remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Mo remonstrated as follows:

sentences.zh: 臣聞治國家者，先資於德義；

translations.literal: I have heard that those who govern a state first rely on virtue and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that governing a state depends first on virtue and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 德義不修，家邦必壞。

translations.literal: if virtue and righteousness are not cultivated, family and state will surely fall to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: if virtue and righteousness are not cultivated, family and state will surely be ruined.

sentences.zh: 故王者以德服人，以義使人。

translations.literal: Therefore a king makes people submit through virtue and moves them through righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a ruler wins submission through virtue and moves people through righteousness.

sentences.zh: 服使之術，要在修身；

translations.literal: The method of making them submit and obey lies above all in self-cultivation;
translations.idiomatic: The means of winning obedience lies above all in self-cultivation;

sentences.zh: 修身之道，在於孜孜。

translations.literal: the way of self-cultivation lies in unceasing effort.
translations.idiomatic: and the way of self-cultivation lies in unceasing effort.

sentences.zh: 夫一失百虧之戒，存乎久要之源。

translations.literal: The warning that one slip leads to a hundred losses resides in the enduring foundation of long-lasting commitment.
translations.idiomatic: The warning that one lapse leads to a hundred failures rests on the enduring foundation of constancy.

sentences.zh: 前志曰：「勿以小惡而為之，勿以小善而不為。」

translations.literal: Earlier writings say, "Do not commit a small evil; do not leave a small good undone."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier writings say, "Do not commit a small evil; do not leave a small good undone."

sentences.zh: 斯則懼於漸也！

translations.literal: This is to fear gradual decline!
translations.idiomatic: That is to fear gradual decline!

sentences.zh: 臣又聞，君如日焉，顯晦之微，人皆瞻仰；

translations.literal: I further hear that the ruler is like the sun — even slight variations of brightness and shadow, all people gaze upon them;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the ruler is like the sun: even the slightest change in light and shadow, all people observe;

sentences.zh: 照臨之大，何以掩藏？

translations.literal: the extent of its illumination — how can it be concealed?
translations.idiomatic: and the breadth of its illumination — how can it be hidden?

sentences.zh: 前代設敢諫之鼓，立誹謗之木，貴聞其過也。

translations.literal: Former ages set up the drum for daring remonstrance and erected the wood for reporting faults, valuing the hearing of one's errors.
translations.idiomatic: Former ages set up the drum for bold remonstrance and the post for reporting faults because they valued hearing of their errors.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來，誕敷文德，不悅聲色，出後宮之怨婦，配在外之鰥夫。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession, you have broadly spread civil virtue, taken no delight in music and women, released aggrieved women from the rear palace, and matched them with widowers outside.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession you have spread civil virtue abroad, taken no delight in music and women, released aggrieved women from the inner palace, and matched them with widowers outside.

sentences.zh: 洎今十年，未嘗采擇。

translations.literal: Down to the present ten years, you have never selected concubines.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years now you have never selected concubines.

sentences.zh: 自數月已來，天睠稍回，留神妓樂，教坊百人、二百人，選試未已；

translations.literal: Since several months ago, Heaven's favor has slightly turned; you have turned attention to courtesans and music — one hundred, two hundred persons from the Music Bureau, selection and testing not yet ended;
translations.idiomatic: But in recent months Heaven's favor has shifted; you have turned your attention to performers and music, with one hundred or two hundred persons from the Music Bureau still under selection and trial;

sentences.zh: 莊宅司收市，亹癖有聞。

translations.literal: the Estate Bureau's purchases on the market — a persistent fondness has been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: and the Estate Bureau's purchases in the markets show a persistent indulgence that has become widely known.

sentences.zh: 昨又宣取李孝本之女入內。

translations.literal: Yesterday an order was issued to take Li Xiaoben's daughter into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday an order was issued to bring Li Xiaoben's daughter into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 宗姓不異，寵幸何名？

translations.literal: She shares the imperial surname — by what name is favor shown?
translations.idiomatic: She bears the imperial surname — by what title is such favor justified?

sentences.zh: 此事深累慎修，有虧一簣。

translations.literal: This matter deeply burdens careful self-cultivation and falls short by one basketful of earth.
translations.idiomatic: This affair deeply undermines careful self-cultivation and leaves the work one basket short of completion.

sentences.zh: 陛下九重之內，不得聞知。

translations.literal: Within Your Majesty's ninefold inner palace, such matters ought not to have escaped your knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Within Your Majesty's inner palace, such matters should not have escaped your notice.

sentences.zh: 凡此之流，大生物議，實傷理道之本，未免塵穢之嫌。

translations.literal: All such matters greatly give rise to public criticism, truly harm the root of governing principle, and cannot escape the taint of defilement.
translations.idiomatic: All such conduct gives rise to widespread criticism, truly injures the foundations of good government, and cannot escape the stain of impropriety.

sentences.zh: 夫欲人不知，莫若勿為。

translations.literal: If one wishes others not to know, there is nothing better than not doing it.
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes others not to know, the best course is not to do it at all.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「止寒莫若重裘，止謗莫若自修。」

translations.literal: A proverb says, "To stop cold, nothing beats a heavy fur; to stop slander, nothing beats self-reform."
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says, "To stop cold, nothing beats a heavy fur; to stop slander, nothing beats self-reform."

sentences.zh: 伏希陛下照鑒不惑；

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will reflect and not be misled;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will reflect clearly and not be misled;

sentences.zh: 崇千載之盛德，去一旦之玩好。

translations.literal: uphold virtue lasting a thousand ages, and cast off momentary indulgences.
translations.idiomatic: uphold virtue that will endure for a thousand years, and cast off passing indulgences.

sentences.zh: 教坊停息，宗女遣還，則大正人倫之風，深弘王者之體。

translations.literal: If the Music Bureau's activities cease and the clanswoman is sent back, then human relations will be greatly set right and the kingly form deeply upheld.
translations.idiomatic: If the Music Bureau's activities cease and the clanswoman is sent home, human relations will be greatly set right and the dignity of kingship deeply upheld.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝即日出孝本女，遷謩右補闕。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor that same day released Xiaoben's daughter and promoted Mo to Right Supplementation Aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor released Xiaoben's daughter that same day and promoted Mo to Right Supplementation Aide.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔乃先祖貞觀中諫書十上，指事直言，無所避諱。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In former times your ancestor in the Zhenguan era submitted remonstrances ten times, addressing matters directly without evasion or concealment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "In former times your ancestor in the Zhenguan era submitted ten remonstrances, speaking directly to the matter without evasion.

sentences.zh: 每覽國史，未嘗不沈吟伸卷，嘉尚久之。

translations.literal: Whenever I peruse the national history, I never fail to ponder deeply and unroll the scroll, admiring him long.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read the national history, I always pause over the scroll and admire him at length.

sentences.zh: 爾為拾遺，其風不墜，屢獻章疏，必道其所以。

translations.literal: You serve as Reminder; that spirit has not fallen. Repeatedly submitting memorials, you always state your reasons.
translations.idiomatic: You serve as Reminder, and that spirit has not declined. In your repeated memorials you always explain your reasons.

sentences.zh: 至於備灑掃於諸王，非自廣其聲妓也；

translations.literal: As for preparing sweepers for the princes, that is not to enlarge one's own troupe of performers;
translations.idiomatic: As for preparing attendants for the princes, that was not to enlarge your own troupe of performers;

sentences.zh: 恤髫齔之宗女，固無嫌於徵取也。

translations.literal: showing concern for a young clanswoman — there is indeed no impropriety in taking her in.
translations.idiomatic: and showing concern for a young clanswoman — there was indeed no impropriety in taking her in.

sentences.zh: 雖然，疑似之間，不可家至而戶曉。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, in matters of suspicion, one cannot visit every household to make all understand.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, in matters of suspicion one cannot make every household understand.

sentences.zh: 爾能詞旨深切，是博我之意多也。

translations.literal: You can make your language earnest and penetrating — you have greatly enlarged my understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Your language is earnest and penetrating, and you have greatly broadened my understanding.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 人能匪躬謇諤，似其先祖；

translations.literal: A man can devote himself without reserve to straight remonstrance, resembling his ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: When a man can devote himself to blunt remonstrance like his ancestor,

sentences.zh: 吾豈不能虛懷延納，仰希貞觀之理歟？

translations.literal: how could I fail to open my mind and accept counsel, looking up to the governance of the Zhenguan era?
translations.idiomatic: how can I fail to open my mind and accept counsel, looking up to the governance of the Zhenguan era?

sentences.zh: 而謩居官日淺，未當敘進，吾豈限以常典，以待直臣！

translations.literal: Yet Mo's time in office is short and he is not yet due for promotion by regular rule — how could I be bound by ordinary precedent in treating a forthright minister!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Mo has served only briefly and is not yet due for promotion by regular rule — how can I be bound by ordinary precedent in treating a forthright minister!

sentences.zh: 可右補闕。」

translations.literal: He is appointed Right Supplementation Aide."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Right Supplementation Aide."

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰臣曰：「昔太宗皇帝得魏徵，裨補闕失，弼成聖政。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chief ministers: "Formerly Emperor Taizong obtained Wei Zheng, who remedied omissions and faults and helped complete sagely governance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the chief ministers, "Formerly Emperor Taizong obtained Wei Zheng, who remedied omissions and faults and helped complete sagely governance.

sentences.zh: 我得魏謩，於疑似之間，必能極諫。

translations.literal: I have obtained Wei Mo; in matters of suspicion he will surely remonstrate to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: I have obtained Wei Mo, who in doubtful matters will surely remonstrate to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 不敢希貞觀之政，庶幾處無過之地矣。」

translations.literal: I dare not hope for the governance of Zhenguan, but perhaps I may stand in a place without fault."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not hope for the governance of the Zhenguan era, but perhaps I may yet stand without fault."

sentences.zh: 教坊副使雲朝霞善吹笛，新聲變律，深愜上旨。

translations.literal: Yun Zhaoxia, deputy director of the Music Bureau, was skilled at playing the flute; his new tunes altered the modes and deeply pleased the emperor's taste.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Zhaoxia, deputy director of the Music Bureau, was skilled at the flute; his new tunes changed the modes and deeply pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 自左驍衛將軍宣授兼揚府司馬。

translations.literal: From Left Brave Guards General an order appointed him concurrently as Yang prefecture Vice Military Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as Left Brave Guards General he was ordered appointed concurrently as Vice Military Administrator of Yang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏曰：「揚府司馬品高，郎官刺史叠處，不可授伶官。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers submitted, "The Vice Military Administrator of Yang prefecture is a high post held in succession by palace officials and prefects. It must not be granted to a performer."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers submitted, "The Vice Military Administrator of Yang prefecture is a high post held in succession by palace officials and prefects. It must not be granted to a performer."

sentences.zh: 上意欲授之，因宰臣對，亟稱朝霞之善。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to grant it; when the chief ministers responded, he repeatedly praised Zhaoxia's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still wished to grant the post, and when the chief ministers replied he repeatedly praised Zhaoxia's talent.

sentences.zh: 謩聞之，累疏陳論，乃改授潤州司馬。

translations.literal: When Mo heard of it, he submitted memorials repeatedly arguing the point; the appointment was then changed to Run prefecture Vice Military Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo heard of this, he submitted repeated memorials arguing against it, and the appointment was changed to Vice Military Administrator of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 荊南監軍使呂令琮從人，擅入江陵縣，毀罵縣令韓忠，觀察使韋長申狀與樞密使訴之。

translations.literal: Jingnan military commissioner Lü Lingcong's followers on their own authority entered Jiangling county, slandered and reviled County Magistrate Han Zhong; Observation Commissioner Wei Chang submitted a petition and complained to the Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The followers of Jingnan military commissioner Lü Lingcong entered Jiangling county without authorization and reviled County Magistrate Han Zhong. Observation Commissioner Wei Chang submitted a report and appealed to the Military Affairs Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 謩上疏曰：「伏以州縣侵屈，只合上聞。

translations.literal: Mo submitted a memorial saying: "I respectfully note that when prefectures and counties suffer wrong, it should only be reported upward to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Mo submitted a memorial saying, "When prefectures and counties suffer wrong, the matter should be reported only to the throne.

sentences.zh: 中外關連，須存舊制。

translations.literal: Internal and external connections must preserve the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Relations between the court and the provinces must follow the established system.

sentences.zh: 韋長任膺廉使，體合精詳，公事都不奏聞，私情擅為逾越。

translations.literal: Wei Chang held the office of integrity commissioner and ought in duty to be precise and thorough; he reported none of the official business but on private feeling on his own authority overstepped protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chang held the post of integrity commissioner and should have been precise and thorough in duty, yet he reported none of the official business and on private impulse overstepped protocol on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 況事無巨細，不可將迎。

translations.literal: Moreover, matters whether great or small must not be handled with favor-currying.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, matters great and small must not be handled through personal favor.

sentences.zh: 縣令官業有乖，便宜理罪；

translations.literal: If the county magistrate's official conduct was faulty, he should conveniently be punished according to law;
translations.idiomatic: If the county magistrate's official conduct was at fault, he should be punished according to law;

sentences.zh: 監軍職司侵越，即合聞天。

translations.literal: if the military commissioner's duty was overstepped, that should be reported to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: if the military commissioner's authority was overstepped, that should be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 或以慮煩聖聽，何不但申門下？

translations.literal: If one feared troubling the sage's hearing, why not simply report through the Secretariat?
translations.idiomatic: If one feared troubling the emperor's attention, why not simply report through the Secretariat?

sentences.zh: 今則首紊常典，理合糾繩。

translations.literal: Now he has first disordered regular precedent and should by principle be censured and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: As it is, he has first violated regular precedent and should by rights be censured and punished.

sentences.zh: 伏望聖慈，速加懲戒！」
