translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will swiftly impose punishment!"
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will swiftly impose punishment!"

sentences.zh: 疏奏不出，時論惜之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it was not issued; contemporaries regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted it was not acted upon, and contemporaries regretted it.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉起居舍人。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Diarist of Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Diarist of Imperial Audience.

sentences.zh: 紫宸中謝，帝謂之曰：「以卿論事忠切，有文貞之風，故不循月限，授卿此官。」

translations.literal: At an audience of thanks in Zichen Hall, the emperor said to him, "Because you discuss affairs with loyal earnestness and have the spirit of Duke Wen Zhen, I do not wait for the usual term and grant you this office."
translations.idiomatic: At an audience of thanks in Zichen Hall, the emperor said to him, "Because you discuss affairs with loyal earnestness and have the spirit of Duke Wen Zhen, I do not wait for the usual term and grant you this office."

sentences.zh: 又謂之曰：「卿家有何舊書詔？」

translations.literal: He also said to him: "What old books and edicts does your family possess?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked him, "What old books and edicts does your family possess?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「比多失墜，惟簪笏見存。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Recently many have been lost; only the court cap and tablet remain."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Many have been lost in recent years; only the court cap and tablet remain."

sentences.zh: 上令進來。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them brought in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them brought in.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「在人不在笏。」

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said, "It lies in the person, not in the tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "It lies in the person, not in the tablet."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「鄭覃不會我意，此即《甘棠》之義，非在笏而已。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zheng Tan does not understand my meaning. This is the meaning of Sweet Pear Tree; it is not merely about the tablet."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zheng Tan does not understand my meaning. This is the meaning of Sweet Pear Tree; it is not merely about the tablet."

sentences.zh: 謩將退，又召誡之曰：「事有不當，即須奏論。」

translations.literal: As Mo was about to withdraw, he was summoned back and admonished, saying: "When something is not appropriate, you must immediately submit memorial and discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: As Mo was about to withdraw, the emperor summoned him back and admonished him: "When something is not appropriate, you must immediately submit a memorial and discuss it."

sentences.zh: 謩曰：「臣頃為諫官，合伸規諷。

translations.literal: Mo said: "Your subject was recently a remonstrance official; it was fitting to present remonstrance and indirect criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Mo said, "Your subject was recently a remonstrance official; it was fitting to offer remonstrance and indirect criticism.

sentences.zh: 今居史職，職在記言，臣不敢輒逾職分。」

translations.literal: Now I hold a historiographer's post; my duty is to record words. Your subject dares not rashly exceed the bounds of my office."
translations.idiomatic: Now I hold a historiographer's post; my duty is to record words. Your subject dares not rashly exceed the bounds of my office."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「凡兩省官並合論事，勿拘此言。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "All officials of the two departments should discuss affairs; do not be bound by these words."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "All officials of the two departments should discuss affairs; do not be bound by these words."

sentences.zh: 尋以本官直弘文館。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, in his existing office he served at the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, in his existing office he served at the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜諫議大夫，仍兼起居舍人，判弘文館事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Remonstrance Grand Master, still concurrently serving as Diarist of Attendance, and given charge of Hongwen Institute affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was appointed Remonstrance Grand Master, still concurrently serving as Diarist of Attendance, and given charge of Hongwen Institute affairs.

sentences.zh: 紫宸入閣，遣中使取謩起居註，欲視之。

translations.literal: During an entrance into the Privy Hall at Zichen Hall, the emperor sent a palace messenger to fetch Mo's diary of imperial attendance, wishing to view it.
translations.idiomatic: During an entrance into the Privy Hall at Zichen Hall, the emperor sent a palace messenger to fetch Mo's diary of imperial attendance, wishing to view it.

sentences.zh: 謩執奏曰：「自古置史官，書事以明鑒誡。

translations.literal: Mo firmly submitted, saying: "Since antiquity historiographers have been established to record events so as to provide clear mirrors and warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Mo firmly submitted, saying, "Since antiquity historiographers have been established to record events so as to provide clear mirrors and warnings.

sentences.zh: 陛下但為善事，勿畏臣不書。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only do good deeds; do not fear that your subject will fail to record them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need only do good deeds; do not fear that your subject will fail to record them.

sentences.zh: 如陛下所行錯忤，臣縱不書，天下之人書之。

translations.literal: If what Your Majesty does is wrong or contrary, even if your subject does not record it, the people of the realm will record it.
translations.idiomatic: If what Your Majesty does is wrong or contrary, even if your subject does not record it, the people of the realm will record it.

sentences.zh: 臣以陛下為文皇帝，陛下比臣如褚遂良。」

translations.literal: Your subject takes Your Majesty to be Emperor Wen; Your Majesty compares your subject to Chu Suiliang."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject takes Your Majesty to be Emperor Wen; Your Majesty compares your subject to Chu Suiliang."

sentences.zh: 帝又曰：「我嘗取觀之。」

translations.literal: The emperor again said: "I once had it taken and viewed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again said, "I once had it taken and viewed."

sentences.zh: 謩曰：「由史官不守職分，臣豈敢陷陛下為非法？

translations.literal: Mo said: "Because the historiographer failed to keep to his office, how could your subject dare to entrap Your Majesty in illegality?
translations.idiomatic: Mo said, "Because the historiographer failed to keep to his office, how could your subject dare to entrap Your Majesty in illegality?

sentences.zh: 陛下一覽之後，自此書事須有回避。

translations.literal: After Your Majesty has once viewed it, from then on recording affairs will require evasion.
translations.idiomatic: After Your Majesty has once viewed it, from then on recording affairs will require evasion.

sentences.zh: 如此，善惡不直，非史也。

translations.literal: In this way, good and evil will not be recorded directly; this is not historiography.
translations.idiomatic: In this way, good and evil will not be recorded directly; this is not historiography.

sentences.zh: 遺後代，何以取信？」

translations.literal: Left to later generations, how will trust be gained?"
translations.idiomatic: Left to later generations, how will trust be gained?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 初立朝，為李固言、李玨、楊嗣復所引，數年之內，至諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When he first entered court, he was promoted by Li Guyan, Li Jue, and Yang Sifu; within several years he reached Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered court, he was promoted by Li Guyan, Li Jue, and Yang Sifu; within several years he reached Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，李德裕用事，謩坐楊、李之黨，出為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Li Deyu held power; Mo was implicated as a member of the Yang and Li faction and was sent out as prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Li Deyu held power; Mo was implicated as a member of the Yang and Li faction and was sent out as prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊、李貶官，謩亦貶信州長史。

translations.literal: When Yang and Li were demoted, Mo was also demoted to chief administrator of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang and Li were demoted, Mo was also demoted to chief administrator of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，白敏中當國，量移郢州刺史，尋換商州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Bai Minzhong directed the state; Mo was transferred to prefect of Yingzhou, and soon after exchanged to Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Bai Minzhong directed the state; Mo was transferred to prefect of Yingzhou, and soon after exchanged to Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，內徵為給事中，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was summoned internally to be Supervising Secretary and was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was summoned internally to serve as Supervising Secretary and was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 謝日，面賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: On the day of his thanksgiving audience, he was granted in person the gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his thanksgiving audience, he was granted in person the gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 彈駙馬都尉杜中立贓罪，貴戚憚之。

translations.literal: He impeached the Commandant-in-Chief of Escort Cavalry Du Zhongli for corrupt offenses; the imperial relatives feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the Commandant-in-Chief of Escort Cavalry Du Zhongli for corrupt offenses; the imperial relatives feared him.

sentences.zh: 兼戶部侍郎，判本司事。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Vice Minister of Revenue and presided over that ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as Vice Minister of Revenue and presided over that ministry's affairs.

sentences.zh: 謩奏曰：「御史臺紀綱之地，不宜與泉貨吏雜處，乞罷中司，專綜戶部公事。」

translations.literal: Mo submitted, saying, "The Censorate is a place of discipline and order; it is not suitable to be mixed with currency officials. I request to be relieved of the censorate office and to devote myself exclusively to the public affairs of the Ministry of Revenue."
translations.idiomatic: Mo submitted, saying, "The Censorate is a place of discipline and order; it is not suitable to be mixed with currency officials. I request to be relieved of the censorate office and to devote myself exclusively to the public affairs of the Ministry of Revenue."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官同平章事，判使如故。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, with his existing office he became Co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery; his commission as commissioner remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, with his existing office he became Co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery; his commission as commissioner remained as before.

sentences.zh: 謝日，奏曰：「臣無夔、契之才，驟叨夔、契之任，將何以仰報鴻私？

translations.literal: On the day of his thanksgiving audience, he submitted, saying: "Your subject lacks the talents of Kui and Qi; yet I have suddenly received the duties of Kui and Qi. With what shall I repay Your Majesty's vast grace?
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his thanksgiving audience, he submitted, saying, "Your subject lacks the talents of Kui and Qi; yet I have suddenly received the duties of Kui and Qi. With what shall I repay Your Majesty's vast grace?

sentences.zh: 今邊戍粗安，海內寧息，臣愚所切者，陛下未立東宮，俾正人傳導，以存副貳之重。」

translations.literal: At present the frontier garrisons are roughly secure and the realm within the seas is at peace. What your subject's foolish heart urgently cares about is that Your Majesty has not yet established the Eastern Palace; let upright men guide and instruct the heir, so as to preserve the weight of the office of deputy and successor."
translations.idiomatic: At present the frontier garrisons are roughly secure and the realm within the seas is at peace. What your subject's foolish heart urgently cares about is that Your Majesty has not yet established the Eastern Palace; let upright men guide and instruct the heir, so as to preserve the weight of the office of deputy and successor."

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: He wept as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 上感而聽之。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and heeded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and heeded him.

sentences.zh: 先是，累朝人君不欲人言立儲貳，若非人主己欲，臣下不敢獻言。

translations.literal: Previously, across successive reigns sovereigns did not wish people to speak of establishing the heir apparent; unless the ruler himself wished it, subordinates did not dare to offer counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, across successive reigns sovereigns did not wish people to speak of establishing the heir apparent; unless the ruler himself wished it, subordinates did not dare to offer counsel.

sentences.zh: 宣宗春秋高，嫡嗣未辨，謩作相之日，率先啟奏，人士重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was advanced in years and the legitimate successor was not yet settled; on the day Mo became chancellor, he was the first to open memorial on the matter, and men of standing regarded him highly for it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was advanced in years and the legitimate successor was not yet settled; on the day Mo became chancellor, he was the first to open memorial on the matter, and men of standing regarded him highly for it.

sentences.zh: 尋兼集賢大學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he concurrently served as Grand Academician of the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he concurrently served as Grand Academician of the Jixian Academy.

sentences.zh: 詹毗國獻象，謩以其性不安中土，請還其使，從之。

translations.literal: Zhanbi presented an elephant; Mo, because elephants are by nature ill-suited to the Central Land, requested that the envoy be sent back, and his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanbi presented an elephant; Mo, because elephants are by nature ill-suited to the Central Land, requested that the envoy be sent back, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 太原節度使李業殺降虜，北邊大擾。

translations.literal: The military governor of Taiyuan, Li Ye, killed surrendered captives, and the northern frontier was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor of Taiyuan, Li Ye, killed surrendered captives, and the northern frontier was greatly disturbed.

sentences.zh: 業有所恃，人不敢非。

translations.literal: Li Ye had someone to rely on; people did not dare criticize him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye had someone to rely on; people did not dare criticize him.

sentences.zh: 謩即奏其事，乃移業滑州。

translations.literal: Mo immediately memorialized on the matter, and Li Ye was transferred to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mo immediately memorialized on the matter, and Li Ye was transferred to Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 加中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice President of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice President of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大理卿馬曙從人王慶告曙家藏兵甲。

translations.literal: Wang Qing, a retainer of Minister of Justice Ma Shu, reported that Ma's household concealed weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qing, a retainer of Minister of Justice Ma Shu, reported that Ma's household concealed weapons and armor.

sentences.zh: 曙坐貶官，而慶無罪。

translations.literal: Ma Shu was demoted for it, yet Qing was found not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shu was demoted for it, yet Qing was found not guilty.

sentences.zh: 謩引法律論之，竟杖殺慶。

translations.literal: Mo cited the law in argument and had Qing beaten to death in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Mo cited the law in argument and had Qing beaten to death in the end.

sentences.zh: 進階銀青光祿大夫，兼禮部尚書、監修國史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in rank to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently serving as Minister of Rites and Overseer of Compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in rank to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently serving as Minister of Rites and Overseer of Compilation of the National History.

sentences.zh: 修成《文宗實錄》四十卷，上之。

translations.literal: He completed compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong in forty fascicles and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He completed compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong in forty fascicles and presented them.

sentences.zh: 其修史官給事中盧耽、太常少卿蔣偕、司勛員外郎王諷、右補闕盧告、膳部員外郎牛叢，皆頒賜錦彩、銀器，序遷職秩。

translations.literal: The historiographers who compiled it—Supervising Secretary Lu Dan, Vice Minister of Rites Jiang Xie, Outer Assisting Director of Merit Wang Feng, Right Reminder Lu Gao, and Outer Assisting Director of Provisions Niu Cong—were all given gifts of brocade and silk and silver vessels, and were promoted in order of rank.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographers who compiled it—Supervising Secretary Lu Dan, Vice Minister of Rites Jiang Xie, Outer Assisting Director of Merit Wang Feng, Right Reminder Lu Gao, and Outer Assisting Director of Provisions Niu Cong—were all given gifts of brocade and silk and silver vessels, and were promoted in order of rank.

sentences.zh: 謩轉門下侍郎，兼戶部尚書，

translations.literal: Mo was transferred to Vice President of the Chancellery and concurrently served as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was transferred to Vice President of the Chancellery and concurrently served as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大中十年，以本官平章事、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使知節度事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dazhong, With his existing office as Co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, he was appointed Governor of Chengdu, Vice Commissioner of the Jiannan West Circuit military governorship with authority over military governorship affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Dazhong, With his existing office as Co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, he was appointed Governor of Chengdu, Vice Commissioner of the Jiannan West Circuit military governorship with authority over military governorship affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以疾求代，徵拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on account of illness he requested replacement; he was summoned and appointed Minister of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, on account of illness he requested replacement; he was summoned and appointed Minister of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 以疾未痊，乞授散秩，改檢校右僕射，守太子少保。

translations.literal: Because his illness had not yet healed, he requested a nominal rank; he was changed to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Acting Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Because his illness had not yet healed, he requested a nominal rank; he was changed to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Acting Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十二年十二月卒，時年六十六，贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, he died, aged sixty-six; he was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, he died, aged sixty-six; he was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 謩儀容魁偉，言論切直，與同列上前言事，他宰相必委曲規諷，唯謩讜言無所畏避。

translations.literal: Mo's bearing was imposing and grand, and his speech was blunt and direct. When he spoke on affairs before the throne together with his fellow chancellors, the other chancellors would invariably use roundabout indirect remonstrance, but Mo alone spoke forthright remonstrance without fear or evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's bearing was imposing and grand, and his speech was blunt and direct. When he spoke on affairs before the throne together with his fellow chancellors, the other chancellors would invariably use roundabout indirect remonstrance, but Mo alone spoke forthright remonstrance without fear or evasion.

sentences.zh: 宣宗每曰：「魏謩綽有祖風，名公子孫，我心重之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong often said, "Wei Mo abundantly possesses his ancestors' manner; he is the scion of a great noble house—my heart holds him in high regard."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong often said, "Wei Mo abundantly possesses his ancestors' manner; he is the scion of a great noble house—my heart holds him in high regard."

sentences.zh: 然竟以語辭太剛，為令狐綯所忌，罷之。

translations.literal: Yet in the end, because his language was too stern, he was resented by Linghu Tao and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end, because his language was too stern, he was resented by Linghu Tao and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 謩嘗鈔撮子書要言，以類相從，二十卷，號曰《魏氏手略》。

translations.literal: Mo once copied and selected essential passages from various books, arranging them by category into twenty fascicles, entitled Wei Family Hand Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: Mo once copied and selected essential passages from various books, arranging them by category into twenty fascicles, entitled Wei Family Hand Compendium.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He had collected writings in ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子潛、滂。

translations.literal: His sons were Qian and Pang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Qian and Pang.

sentences.zh: 潛登進士第。

translations.literal: Qian passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Qian passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 潛子敖，韋琮甥。

translations.literal: Qian's son Ao was the nephew of Wei Cong on his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Ao was the nephew of Wei Cong on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 後琮為相，潛歷顯官。

translations.literal: Later, when Cong became chancellor, Qian held successive prominent offices.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Cong became chancellor, Qian held successive prominent offices.

sentences.zh: 周墀，字德升，汝南人。

translations.literal: Zhou Chi—Zhou Chi, courtesy name Desheng, was a native of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi—Zhou Chi, courtesy name Desheng, was a native of Runan.

sentences.zh: 祖颋，父霈。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Ting; his father was Pei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Ting; his father was Pei.

sentences.zh: 墀，長慶二年擢進士第，太和末，累遷至起居郎。

translations.literal: Chi passed the jinshi examination in Changqing year two; at the end of the Taihe era he was promoted through successive posts to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Chi passed the jinshi examination in Changqing year two; at the end of the Taihe era he was promoted through successive posts to Diarist.

sentences.zh: 墀能為古文，有史才。

translations.literal: Chi could write ancient-style prose and possessed talent for history.
translations.idiomatic: Chi could write ancient-style prose and possessed talent for history.

sentences.zh: 文宗重之，補集賢學士，轉考功員外郎，仍兼起居舍人事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong valued him; he was appointed Academician of the Jixian Academy, transferred to Outer Assisting Director of Merit, and still concurrently held the post of Diarist of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong valued him; he was appointed Academician of the Jixian Academy, transferred to Outer Assisting Director of Merit, and still concurrently held the post of Diarist of Attendance.

sentences.zh: 開成二年冬，以本官知制誥，尋召充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng, in winter, with his existing office he was made Drafting Secretary; soon after he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaicheng, in winter, with his existing office he was made Drafting Secretary; soon after he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷職方郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，正拜中書舍人，內職如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year, he was formally appointed Secretary of the Secretariat; his inner-court duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year, he was formally appointed Secretary of the Secretariat; his inner-court duties remained as before.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，出為華州刺史、鎮國軍潼關防禦等使，改鄂州刺史、御史中丞、鄂嶽觀察使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, he was sent out as prefect of Huazhou and Commissioner of Defense of Tong Pass for the Zhenguo Army; he was changed to prefect of Ezhou, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Observation Commissioner of E and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, he was sent out as prefect of Huazhou and Commissioner of Defense of Tong Pass for the Zhenguo Army; he was changed to prefect of Ezhou, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Observation Commissioner of E and Yue.

sentences.zh: 會昌六年十一月，遷洪州刺史、江南西道觀察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Huichang, in the eleventh month, he was transferred to prefect of Hongzhou and Observation Commissioner of the Jiangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Huichang, in the eleventh month, he was transferred to prefect of Hongzhou and Observation Commissioner of the Jiangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大中初，檢校禮部尚書、滑州刺史、義成軍節度、鄭滑觀察等使、上柱國、汝南男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong era, he was Acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Hua Prefecture, military governor of the Yicheng Army, Commissioner of Observation for Zheng and Hua, Pillars of the State of the First Rank, Duke of Runan, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazhong era, he was Acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Hua Prefecture, military governor of the Yicheng Army, Commissioner of Observation for Zheng and Hua, Pillars of the State of the First Rank, Duke of Runan, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 入朝為兵部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of War and presided over the Department of Public Works and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Minister of War and presided over the Department of Public Works and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官同平章事，累遷銀青光祿大夫、中書侍郎、監修國史，兼刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, with his existing office he became Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery; he was promoted in succession to Glorious Grand Master with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, Director of National History, and concurrently Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, with his existing office he became Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery; he was promoted in succession to Glorious Grand Master with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, Director of National History, and concurrently Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 罷相，檢校刑部尚書、梓州刺史、御史大夫、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: Dismissed as chancellor, he was Acting Minister of Justice, prefect of Zizhou, Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed as chancellor, he was Acting Minister of Justice, prefect of Zizhou, Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 未行，追制改檢校右僕射，加食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Before he departed, a follow-up edict changed his appointment to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and added five hundred households to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, a follow-up edict changed his appointment to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and added five hundred households to his fief.

sentences.zh: 歷方鎮卒。

translations.literal: He served in regional commands and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He served in regional commands and died there.

sentences.zh: 崔龜從，字玄告，清河人。

translations.literal: Cui Guicong—Cui Guicong, courtesy name Xuangao, was a native of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guicong—Cui Guicong, courtesy name Xuangao, was a native of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖璜，父誠，官微。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Huang; his father was Cheng; both held minor offices.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Huang; his father was Cheng; both held minor offices.

sentences.zh: 龜從，元和十二年擢進士第，又登賢良方正制科，及書判拔萃二科，釋褐拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: Guicong passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year twelve, also passed the decree examination for Worthy and Upright men, as well as the two examinations of Document Drafting and Outstanding Selection; upon first taking office he was appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year twelve, also passed the decree examination for Worthy and Upright men, as well as the two examinations of Document Drafting and Outstanding Selection; upon first taking office he was appointed Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，改太常博士。

translations.literal: In Taihe year two, he was changed to Erudite of the Grand Sacrifices Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year two, he was changed to Erudite of the Grand Sacrifices Bureau.

sentences.zh: 龜從長於禮學，精歷代沿革，問無不通。

translations.literal: Guicong excelled in the study of rites and was thoroughly versed in the changes through successive dynasties; on whatever was asked, nothing was beyond his knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong excelled in the study of rites and was thoroughly versed in the changes through successive dynasties; on whatever was asked, nothing was beyond his knowledge.

sentences.zh: 時饗宗廟於敬宗室，祝板稱皇帝孝弟。

translations.literal: At that time, when offerings were made in the ancestral temple at the shrine of Emperor Jingzong, the prayer board addressed the emperor as filial and brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, when offerings were made in the ancestral temple at the shrine of Emperor Jingzong, the prayer board addressed the emperor as filial and brotherly.

sentences.zh: 龜從議曰：「臣審祥孝字，載考禮文，義本主於子孫，理難施於兄弟。

translations.literal: Guicong submitted an opinion, saying: "Your subject has carefully examined the character xiao in detail and consulted the ritual texts: its meaning fundamentally belongs to descendants; it is logically difficult to apply to brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong submitted an opinion, saying, "Your subject has carefully examined the character xiao in detail and consulted the ritual texts: its meaning fundamentally belongs to descendants; it is logically difficult to apply to brothers.

sentences.zh: 按《禮記》卜虞之文，子孫曰哀，兄弟曰某。

translations.literal: According to the passage on divination for the yu rite in the Record of Rites, descendants say "grieved"; brothers say "so-and-so."
translations.idiomatic: According to the passage on divination for the yu rite in the Record of Rites, descendants say "grieved"; brothers say "so-and-so."

sentences.zh: 然則虞之稱哀，與祭之稱孝，其義一也。

translations.literal: Thus the yu rite's use of "grieved" and the sacrificial rite's use of "filial" share the same meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the yu rite's use of "grieved" and the sacrificial rite's use of "filial" share the same meaning.

sentences.zh: 於祖禰則理宜稱孝，於伯仲則止可稱名。

translations.literal: Toward grandfathers and fathers it is proper to use "filial"; toward elder and younger brothers one may only use personal names.
translations.idiomatic: Toward grandfathers and fathers it is proper to use "filial"; toward elder and younger brothers one may only use personal names.

sentences.zh: 又東晉溫嶠議宗廟祝辭，於孝字非子者則不稱，傍親直言敢告。

translations.literal: Furthermore, in the Eastern Jin, Wen Jiao debated ancestral temple prayer language: where the character xiao did not apply to a son, it was not used; for collateral relatives one spoke plainly with "I boldly announce."
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, in the Eastern Jin, Wen Jiao debated ancestral temple prayer language: where the character xiao did not apply to a son, it was not used; for collateral relatives one spoke plainly with "I boldly announce."

sentences.zh: 當時朝議，咸以為宜。

translations.literal: At that time the court discussion unanimously deemed it appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court discussion unanimously deemed it appropriate.

sentences.zh: 今臣上考禮經，無兄弟稱孝之義；

translations.literal: Now your subject consults the ritual classics above and finds no rationale for brothers to be called "filial";
translations.idiomatic: Now your subject consults the ritual classics above and finds no rationale for brothers to be called "filial";

sentences.zh: 下徵晉史，有不稱傍親之文。

translations.literal: and below cites Jin history, which has passages not applying "filial" to collateral relatives.
translations.idiomatic: and below cites Jin history, which has passages not applying "filial" to collateral relatives.

sentences.zh: 臣謂饗敬宗廟，宜去孝弟兩字。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that for offerings at Emperor Jingzong's shrine, the two characters xiao and di should be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that for offerings at Emperor Jingzong's shrine, the two characters xiao and di should be removed."

sentences.zh: 又以祀九宮壇，舊是大祠。

translations.literal: He also addressed the sacrifice at the Nine Palaces Altar, which had formerly been a major sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed the sacrifice at the Nine Palaces Altar, which had formerly been a major sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 龜從議曰：「九宮貴神，經典不載。

translations.literal: Guicong submitted an opinion, saying: "The noble spirits of the Nine Palaces are not recorded in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong submitted an opinion, saying, "The noble spirits of the Nine Palaces are not recorded in the classics.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，術士奏請，遂立祠壇。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, geomancers petitioned, and an altar was thereby established.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era, geomancers petitioned, and an altar was thereby established.

sentences.zh: 事出一時，禮同郊祀。

translations.literal: It arose from a moment in time; its ritual was made equal to suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: It arose from a moment in time; its ritual was made equal to suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 臣詳其圖法，皆主星名，縱司水旱兵荒，品秩不過列宿。

translations.literal: Your subject has examined its diagrams and regulations in detail: all are named for chief stars; even if they oversee flood, drought, war, and famine, their ranks do not exceed those of the constellations.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has examined its diagrams and regulations in detail: all are named for chief stars; even if they oversee flood, drought, war, and famine, their ranks do not exceed those of the constellations.

sentences.zh: 今者，五星悉是從祀，日月猶在中祠，豈容九宮獨越常禮，備列王事，誡誓百官？

translations.literal: At present the Five Planets are all ancillary sacrifices; the sun and moon still rank among the middle sacrifices—how can the Nine Palaces alone exceed ordinary ritual, be fully arrayed with the king's affairs, and administer oaths and admonitions to the hundred officials?
translations.idiomatic: At present the Five Planets are all ancillary sacrifices; the sun and moon still rank among the middle sacrifices—how can the Nine Palaces alone exceed ordinary ritual, be fully arrayed with the king's affairs, and administer oaths and admonitions to the hundred officials?

sentences.zh: 尊卑乖儀，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: High and low violate ritual propriety—nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: In the violation of proper order between superior and inferior, nothing goes further than this.

sentences.zh: 若以嘗在祀典，不可廢除，臣請降為中祠。」

translations.literal: If because they were once in the sacrificial canon they cannot be abolished, your subject requests reducing them to middle sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: If, because they were once included in the sacrificial canon, they cannot be abolished entirely, your subject requests that they be reduced to middle sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 制從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 龜從又以大臣薨謝，不於聞哀日輟朝，奏議曰：「伏以廢朝軫悼，義重君臣，所貴及哀，尤宜示信。

translations.literal: Guicong again, because of a great minister's death announcement, when court was not suspended on the day mourning was heard, submitted a memorial opinion, saying: "Your subject considers that suspending court to express grief—the righteousness weighs heavily on lord and minister; what is prized is reaching the moment of grief; it is especially fitting to show sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong also addressed the case of a great minister's death, when court was not suspended on the day the mourning was reported. He submitted a memorial: "Your subject considers that suspending court to express grief is a bond of profound weight between sovereign and minister. The essential point is to respond at the moment grief is felt, and above all to demonstrate sincerity.

sentences.zh: 自頃已來，輟朝非奏報之時，備禮於數日外。

translations.literal: From recent times onward, court suspension has not been at the time of the memorial report; full ritual has been prepared several days later.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times, court has been suspended not at the moment the death is reported, but only after full ceremonial preparations are completed days later.

sentences.zh: 雖遵常制，似不本情。

translations.literal: Although following regular regulations, it seems not rooted in true feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Though this follows established precedent, it seems not to reflect genuine feeling.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢遠徵古書，請引國朝故事：貞觀中任瑰卒，有司對仗奏闕聞，太宗責其乖禮；

translations.literal: Your subject dares not cite distant ancient books; your subject requests citing precedents of our dynasty: in the Zhenguan era when Ren Gui died, the relevant offices reported the death at imperial audience; Taizong reproached them for violating ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject dares not reach back to distant ancient texts and instead cites precedents from our own dynasty: in the Zhenguan era, when Ren Gui died, the relevant offices reported his death at imperial audience, and Emperor Taizong reproached them for violating ritual propriety;

sentences.zh: 岑文本既歿，其夕為罷警嚴；

translations.literal: when Cen Wenben had died, that very evening the strict guard was suspended;
translations.idiomatic: when Cen Wenben died, that very evening the strict palace guard was suspended;

sentences.zh: 張公謹之亡，哭之不避辰日。

translations.literal: when Zhang Gongjin passed away, mourning for him did not avoid the taboo day.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhang Gongjin died, mourning for him was observed without avoiding the day's ritual taboos.

sentences.zh: 是知閔悼之意，不宜過時。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the intent of pity and mourning should not exceed the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that the sentiment of pity and mourning should not be delayed past its proper moment.

sentences.zh: 臣謂大臣薨，禮合輟朝。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that when a great minister dies, ritual propriety requires suspending court.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that when a great minister dies, ritual propriety requires that court be suspended.

sentences.zh: 縱有機務急速，便殿須召宰臣，不臨正朝，無爽事體。

translations.literal: Even if urgent state affairs are pressing, the side hall requires summoning the chief ministers; not attending the main court audience would not compromise the substance of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even if urgent state business demands attention, the sovereign can summon the chief ministers to the side hall; not holding the main court audience would not compromise the substance of government.

sentences.zh: 如此，則由衷之信，載感於幽明；

translations.literal: In this way, then sincere faith from the heart would move both the hidden and the manifest;
translations.idiomatic: In this way, sincere grief from the heart would move both the living and the dead;

sentences.zh: 稱情之文，無虧於典禮。」

translations.literal: words consonant with feeling would not fall short of canonical ritual."
translations.idiomatic: and expressions consonant with genuine feeling would not fall short of canonical ritual."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「文武三品官薨卒輟朝。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "When civil and military officials of the third rank or above die, court should be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized: "When civil and military officials of the third rank or above die, court should be suspended.

sentences.zh: 有未經親重之官，今任又是散列者，為之變禮，誠恐非宜。

translations.literal: There are offices that have never been personally valued; if their present post is additionally a dispersive rank, to alter ritual for them truly seems inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: When the deceased has never held a position of personal trust, and his current post is merely one of ordinary rank, to alter ritual for him truly seems inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 自今後，文武三品以上官，非曾任將相，及曾在密近，宜加恩禮者，餘請不在輟朝之限。」

translations.literal: From now on, for civil and military officials above the third rank, unless they formerly served as general or chief minister, or were once in intimate proximity warranting added gracious ritual, the rest please should not fall within the scope of court suspension."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, for civil and military officials of the third rank and above, unless they formerly served as general or chief minister, or were once in close attendance and deserving of added gracious ritual, the rest should not fall within the scope of court suspension."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 累轉考功郎中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to Director of the Bureau of Merit Evaluation and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to director of the Bureau of Merit Evaluation and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 九年，轉司勛郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Awards and Commendations and was charged with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he was transferred to director of the Bureau of Awards and Commendations and charged with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 十二月，正拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he was formally appointed Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, he was formally appointed secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開成初，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, he was sent out as prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, he was sent out as prefect of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，人為戶部侍郎，判本司事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, he returned to court as Vice Minister of Public Works and Revenue and presided over that department's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year, he returned to court as vice minister of public works and revenue and presided over that department's affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，權判吏部尚書銓事，

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he acted as provisional judge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he acted as provisional judge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection affairs.

sentences.zh: 大中四年，為中書侍郎、同平章事，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong, He was appointed Vice President of the Secretariat, Co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrently Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong, He was appointed vice president of the Secretariat, co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrently minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，撰成《續唐歷》三十卷，上之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year, he completed compilation of the 《Continuation of the Tang Annals》 in thirty volumes and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year, he completed the 《Continuation of the Tang Annals》 in thirty volumes and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 六年，罷相，檢校吏部尚書，汴州刺史、宣武軍節度觀察等使，累歷方鎮卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, dismissed as chancellor, he was Acting Minister of Personnel, prefect of Bian Prefecture, military governor and observation commissioner of the Xuanwu Army, served in successive regional commands, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, dismissed as chancellor, he served as acting minister of personnel, prefect of Bian Prefecture, and military governor and observation commissioner of the Xuanwu Army; he held successive regional commands and died in office.

sentences.zh: 鄭肅，滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Su—Zheng Su was a native of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Su—Zheng Su was a native of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 祖烈，父閱，世儒家。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Lie; his father was Yue; the family were Confucian scholars for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Lie and his father Yue; the family had been Confucian scholars for generations.

sentences.zh: 肅苦心力學，

translations.literal: Su toiled bitterly and studied with all his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Su studied with exhausting diligence and wholehearted devotion.

sentences.zh: 元和三年，擢進士第，又以書判拔萃，歷佐使府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhe, He passed the jinshi examination, also achieved Outstanding Selection in Document Drafting, and served in successive staff posts in prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhe, He passed the jinshi examination, also achieved outstanding selection in document drafting, and served in successive staff posts in prefectural offices.

sentences.zh: 太和初，入朝為尚書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era, he entered court as a Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era, he entered court as a director in one of the secretariat departments.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Sacrifices Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was transferred to vice director of the Grand Sacrifices Bureau.

sentences.zh: 肅能為古文，長於經學，左丘明、《三禮》、儀註疑議，博士以下必就肅決之。

translations.literal: Su could write classical prose and excelled in the study of the classics; on Zuò Qiūmíng, the 《Three Rites》, and doubtful points in ritual commentaries, scholars below the rank of erudite invariably went to Su for final decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Su could write classical prose and excelled in classical learning; on Zuò Qiūmíng, the 《Three Rites》, and doubtful points in ritual commentaries, scholars below the rank of erudite invariably went to Su for a final ruling.

sentences.zh: 時魯王永有寵，文宗擇名儒為其府屬，用戶部侍郎庾敬休兼王傅，戶部郎中李踐方兼司馬，以肅本官兼長史，由是知名。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Yong of Lu enjoyed favor; Emperor Wenzong selected renowned Confucians as staff for his princely establishment, appointing Vice Minister of Public Works and Revenue Yu Jingxiu concurrently as the prince's mentor, Director Yu of the same ministry Li Jianfang concurrently as chief administrator, and Su with his existing office concurrently as chief secretary—thereby becoming renowned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Yong of Lu enjoyed the emperor's favor; Emperor Wenzong selected renowned Confucians as staff for his princely establishment, appointing Vice Minister Yu Jingxiu concurrently as the prince's mentor, Director Li Jianfang of the same ministry concurrently as chief administrator, and Su with his existing office concurrently as chief secretary—through which Su became widely known.

sentences.zh: 明年，魯王為太子，肅加給事中。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Prince of Lu became crown prince, Su was additionally appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Prince of Lu was made crown prince, Su was additionally appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 九年，改刑部侍郎，尋改尚書右丞，權判吏部西銓事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was changed to Vice Minister of Justice; shortly thereafter changed to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and acted as judge of the western board of the Ministry of Personnel's selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he was transferred to vice minister of justice; shortly thereafter he became right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and acted as judge of the western board of the Ministry of Personnel's selection.

sentences.zh: 開成初，出為陜虢都防禦觀察使、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, he was sent out as Commissioner of Defense and Observation for Shan and Guo, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, he was sent out as commissioner of defense and observation for Shan and Guo, concurrently serving as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，召拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year, he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year, he was summoned and appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝以肅嘗侍太子，言論典正，復令兼太子賓客，為東宮授經。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Su had once attended the crown prince and his discourse was canonical and correct, again ordered him to serve concurrently as Mentor to the Crown Prince, instructing the Eastern Palace in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Because Su had once attended the crown prince and his discourse was canonical and upright, the emperor again ordered him to serve concurrently as mentor to the crown prince, teaching the classics in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 既而太子失寵，上不悅，有廢斥意。

translations.literal: Before long the crown prince lost favor; the emperor was displeased and had intent to depose and banish him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the crown prince lost favor; the emperor was displeased and contemplated deposing him.

sentences.zh: 肅因召見，深陳邦國大本、君臣父子之義。

translations.literal: Su then received a summons and audience; he deeply expounded the great foundations of the state and the principles of sovereign and minister, father and son.
translations.idiomatic: When Su was summoned for an audience, he spoke at length on the fundamental principles of the state and the duties binding sovereign and minister, father and son.

sentences.zh: 上改容嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor changed his expression and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression softened and he praised Su.

sentences.zh: 而太子竟以楊妃故得罪。

translations.literal: Yet the crown prince in the end was punished on account of Consort Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end the crown prince was punished on account of Consort Yang.

sentences.zh: 乃以肅檢校禮部尚書，兼河中尹、河中節度、晉絳觀察等使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su was appointed Acting Minister of Rites, concurrently Governor of Hezhong, military governor of Hezhong, and observation commissioner for Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Su was then appointed acting minister of rites, concurrently governor of Hezhong, military governor of Hezhong, and observation commissioner for Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，武宗思太子永之無罪，盡誅陷永之黨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huichang era, Emperor Wuzong reflected that Crown Prince Yong was innocent and executed to the last those who had framed Yong's faction.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huichang era, Emperor Wuzong reflected that Crown Prince Yong had been innocent and executed all those who had framed him and his faction.

sentences.zh: 朝議稱肅忠正，有大臣之節。

translations.literal: Court discussion praised Su as loyal and upright, possessing a great minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion praised Su as loyal and upright, a man of great ministerial integrity.

sentences.zh: 召拜太常卿，累遷戶部、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Director of the Grand Sacrifices Bureau; he was promoted in succession to Minister of Public Works and Revenue and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed director of the Grand Sacrifices Bureau and was promoted in succession to minister of public works and revenue and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 五年，以本官同平章事，加中書、門下二侍郎，監修國史，兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, with his existing office he became Co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was additionally appointed Vice President of both the Secretariat and the Chancellery, Overseer of Compilation of the National History, and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, with his existing office he became co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was additionally appointed vice president of both the Secretariat and the Chancellery, overseer of compilation of the national history, and concurrently right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 素與李德裕親厚。

translations.literal: He had long been close and warm with Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been on close and friendly terms with Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，德裕罷知政事，肅亦罷相，復為河中節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Deyu was dismissed from managing state affairs; Su also was dismissed as chancellor and again became military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Deyu was removed from government; Su was also dismissed as chancellor and again became military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 以疾辭，拜太子太保，卒。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of illness; he was appointed Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince and died.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on account of illness, was appointed grand mentor to the crown prince, and died.

sentences.zh: 子 洎子洎，咸通中累官尚書郎，出為刺史。

translations.literal: His son Ji—Ji, in the Xiantong era accumulated offices as a Director in the Secretariat and was sent out as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji—in the Xiantong era he rose through successive posts as a director in the secretariat and was sent out as prefect.

sentences.zh: 洎子仁規、仁表，俱有俊才，文翰高逸。

translations.literal: Ji's sons Rengui and Renbiao both possessed outstanding talent; their literary writing was lofty and refined.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's sons Rengui and Renbiao both possessed outstanding talent, and their literary writing was lofty and refined.

sentences.zh: 孫 仁規仁規累遷拾遣、補闕、尚書郎、湖州刺史、尚書郎知制誥，正拜中書舍人，卒。

translations.literal: Grandson Rengui—Rengui was promoted in succession to Reminder, Reviser, Director in the Secretariat, prefect of Huzhou, Director in the Secretariat charged with drafting edicts, formally appointed Secretary of the Secretariat, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Rengui rose in succession through the posts of reminder, reviser, and director in the secretariat, served as prefect of Huzhou, then as a director charged with drafting edicts, was formally appointed secretary of the Secretariat, and died.

sentences.zh: 孫 仁表仁表擢第後，從杜審權、趙騭為華州、河中掌書記，入為起居郎。

translations.literal: Grandson Renbiao—After Renbiao passed the examination, he followed Du Shenquan and Zhao Yi as chief secretary at Hua Prefecture and Hezhong, and entered court as Attendant of Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Renbiao, after passing the examination, served as chief secretary under Du Shenquan and Zhao Yi at Hua Prefecture and Hezhong, then entered court as attendant of imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 仁表文章尤稱俊拔，然恃才傲物，人士薄之。

translations.literal: Renbiao's literary writing was especially praised as brilliant and forceful; yet he relied on his talent and looked down on others, and gentlemen disparaged him.
translations.idiomatic: Renbiao's writing was especially praised as brilliant and forceful, yet he relied on his talent and looked down on others, and men of standing held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 自謂門地、人物、文章具美，嘗曰：「天瑞有五色雲，人瑞有鄭仁表。」

translations.literal: He considered himself possessed of family standing, personal character, and literary writing all in perfection, and once said: "Heaven's auspicious sign has the five-colored cloud; man's auspicious sign has Zheng Renbiao."
translations.idiomatic: He considered his family standing, personal character, and literary talent all without peer, and once said, "Heaven's auspicious sign is the five-colored cloud; mankind's auspicious sign is Zheng Renbiao."

sentences.zh: 劉鄴少時，投文於洎，仁表兄弟嗤鄙之。

translations.literal: When Liu Ye was young, he submitted writings to Ji; the Renbiao brothers scorned and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ye was young, he submitted writings to Ji; Renbiao and his brothers scorned and despised him.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，鄴為宰相，仁表竟貶死南荒。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiantong era, Ye became chancellor; Renbiao in the end was banished and died in the southern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xiantong era, Ye became chancellor, and Renbiao was ultimately banished and died in the southern wilds.

sentences.zh: 盧商，字為臣，范陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Shang—Lu Shang, courtesy name Weichen, was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shang—Lu Shang, whose courtesy name was Weichen, was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖昂，灃州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ang was prefect of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ang served as prefect of Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父廣，河南縣尉。

translations.literal: His father Guang was magistrate of Henan County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang served as magistrate of Henan County.

sentences.zh: 商，元和四年擢進士第，又書判拔萃登科。

translations.literal: Shang passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year four and also passed the outstanding selection in document drafting.
translations.idiomatic: Shang passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe year four and also passed the outstanding selection in document drafting.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧力學，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he studied diligently; upon first taking office he was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth and poor, he studied diligently; upon first taking office he was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 範傅式廉察宣歙，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Fan Fushi inspected Xuancheng and She Prefectures, he recruited Shang as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Fushi served as inspector of Xuancheng and She prefectures, he recruited Shang as an aide.

sentences.zh: 王播、段文昌相繼鎮西蜀，商皆佐職為記室，累改禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Wang Bo and Duan Wenchang successively governed western Shu, Shang in each case served as staff secretary; he was changed in succession to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Bo and Duan Wenchang successively governed western Shu, Shang served on each of their staffs as secretary; he was promoted in succession to vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 入朝為工部員外郎、河南縣令，歷工部、度支、司封三郎中，

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Public Works and Magistrate of Henan County; he passed through the three directorships of Public Works, Revenue, and Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as vice director of the Ministry of Public Works and magistrate of Henan County, and served in succession as director of the departments of public works, revenue, and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，改京兆少尹，權大理卿事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe, He was changed to Vice Mayor of Jingzhao and acted as Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taihe, He was transferred to vice mayor of Jingzhao and acted as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 開成初，出為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, he was sent out as prefect of Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, he was sent out as prefect of Su Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中謝日，賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: On the day of his mid-audience thanksgiving, he was granted the gold-and-purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his audience of thanksgiving, he was granted the gold-and-purple ceremonial robe.

sentences.zh: 初，郡人苦鹽法太煩，奸吏侵漁。

translations.literal: Initially, the people of the prefecture suffered that the salt law was too burdensome and corrupt officials exploited them.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the people of the prefecture suffered under an overly burdensome salt law, while corrupt officials exploited them.

sentences.zh: 商至，籍見戶，量所要自售，無定額。

translations.literal: When Shang arrived, he registered and inspected households, measured according to need for self-sale, with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang arrived, he registered households, assessed each family's needs, and allowed them to purchase salt as required, with no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 蘇人便之，歲課增倍。

translations.literal: The people of Su found this convenient; annual revenue doubled.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Su found this convenient, and annual revenue doubled.

sentences.zh: 宰相領鹽鐵，以其績上，遷潤州刺史、浙西團練觀察使。

translations.literal: The chief minister who oversaw salt and iron submitted his achievements; he was transferred to prefect of Run Prefecture and Commissioner of Training and Observation for Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister who oversaw salt and iron submitted report of his achievements, and Shang was transferred to prefect of Run Prefecture and commissioner of training and observation for Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部侍郎，轉京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of Justice and was transferred to Mayor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as vice minister of justice and was transferred to mayor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 三年，朝廷用兵上黨，飛挽越太行者，環地六七鎮，以商為戶部侍郎，判度支，兼供軍使，軍用無闕。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the court deployed troops at Shangdang, rapid transport crossed the Taihang Mountains, encircling six or seven garrison commands in the territory; Shang was appointed Vice Minister of Public Works and Revenue, presided over the Department of Public Works and Revenue, and concurrently served as Army Supply Commissioner; military supplies were without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the court waged war at Shangdang, rapid transport routes crossed the Taihang Mountains through six or seven surrounding garrison commands; Shang was appointed vice minister of public works and revenue, presided over the Department of Public Works and Revenue, and concurrently served as army supply commissioner, and military provisions were never wanting.

sentences.zh: 逆稹蕩平，加檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: When the rebel Zhen was swept away and pacified, Shang was additionally appointed Acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Liu Zhen was suppressed, Shang was additionally appointed acting minister of rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，入為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, he entered court as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, he returned to court as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官同平章事、范陽郡開國公，食邑二千戶，加兼工部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, with his existing office he became Co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Duke of Fanyang Commandery with a fief of two thousand households, and was additionally appointed concurrently Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, with his existing office he became co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang Commandery with a fief of two thousand households, and was additionally appointed minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 數年，檢校工部尚書，出為鄂嶽觀察使，就加檢校兵部尚書，

translations.literal: After several years, he was Acting Minister of Public Works, sent out as Observation Commissioner of E and Yue, and thereupon additionally appointed Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After several years, he served as acting minister of public works, was sent out as observation commissioner of E and Yue, and was thereupon additionally appointed acting minister of war.

sentences.zh: 大中十三年，以疾求代，徵拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dazhong, Due to illness he requested replacement; he was summoned and appointed Minister of Public Works and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Dazhong, Due to illness he requested a replacement in his post; he was summoned and appointed minister of public works and revenue.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，卒於漢陰驛，時年七十一。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year, he died at Hanyin Post; he was then seventy-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year, he died at Hanyin Post at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 子知遠、知微、知宗、僧朗、蕘。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhiyuan, Zhiwei, Zhizong, Senglang, and Rao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhiyuan, Zhiwei, Zhizong, Senglang, and Rao.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：宗閔、嗣復，承宗室世家之地胄，有文學政事之美名，徊翔清華，出入隆顯。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Zongmin and Sifu inherited the lineage of an imperial-clan noble house; they possessed renowned literary and administrative attainments, circled through pure and honored posts, and entered and exited in lofty prominence.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Zongmin and Sifu were heirs to an imperial-clan noble house renowned for literary and administrative excellence; they moved through the highest offices and rose to eminent prominence.

sentences.zh: 茍能義以為上，群而不黨，議太平於稷、契之列，致人主於勛、華之盛，遭時得位，誰曰不然？

translations.literal: If they could have placed righteousness above all, gathered without forming factions, deliberated on great peace among the ranks of Ji and Qi, and brought the sovereign to the splendor of Xun and Hua, encountering the times and gaining position—who would say it was not so?
translations.idiomatic: Had they placed righteousness above all, joined with others without forming factions, deliberated on great peace in the company of Ji and Qi, and guided the sovereign to the glory of Yao and Shun, who encountering fortune and gaining office could say otherwise?

sentences.zh: 而舍披鴻猷，狎茲鼠輩，養虞卿而射利，抗德裕以報仇。

translations.literal: Yet they abandoned spreading the great design, consorted with these rat-like fellows, nourished Yu Qing to shoot for profit, and opposed Deyu to avenge a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they abandoned the great design of state, consorted with contemptible men, cultivated Yu Qing for personal gain, and opposed Deyu to settle an old grudge.

sentences.zh: 矛盾相攻，幾傾王室，沒身蠻瘴，其利伊何？

translations.literal: They attacked each other in mutual contradiction, nearly overturning the royal house; they ended their lives in miasmic barbarian lands—what profit was in that?
translations.idiomatic: They attacked each other relentlessly, nearly bringing down the throne; they ended their lives in the malarial south—what profit did they gain?

sentences.zh: 古者，廉、藺解仇，冀全國體，而邀歡釋憾，實亂大倫。

translations.literal: In antiquity, Lian Po and Lin Xiangru resolved their enmity, hoping to preserve the integrity of the state; but to seek mutual pleasure and release resentment in fact disrupts the great human relationships.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Lian Po and Lin Xiangru set aside their enmity in hope of preserving the integrity of the state; yet to seek mutual favor and release old resentments in fact disrupts the fundamental order of human relations.

sentences.zh: 世道銷刓，一至於此！

translations.literal: The ways of the world wore away and were cut down, reaching to this!
translations.idiomatic: The moral order of the age had decayed to this point!

sentences.zh: 崔、魏二丞相，嘉言啟奏，無忝正人。

translations.literal: The two chief ministers Cui and Wei submitted excellent words to the throne, not unworthy of upright men.
translations.idiomatic: The two chief ministers Cui and Wei offered excellent counsel to the throne, in keeping with the conduct of upright men.

sentences.zh: 墀、讓史才，肅之禮學，商之長者，或登三事，或踐六卿，以道始終，夫何不韙。

translations.literal: Chi and Rang possessed historiographical talent; Su's ritual learning; Shang's elder virtue—some ascended to the Three Affairs, some trod the Six Ministers; beginning and ending with the Way—how could this not be right.
translations.idiomatic: Chi and Rang possessed historiographical talent, Su mastered ritual learning, and Shang was a man of elder virtue; some rose to the highest offices, some served among the six ministers, and all maintained the Way from beginning to end—what could be more fitting.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：漢誅鉤黨，魏破疽囊。

translations.literal: Praise says: Han executed the Partisan Proscription; Wei burst the abscess pouch.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Han executed the Partisan Proscription; Wei lanced the abscess.

sentences.zh: 何鄧之後，二李三楊。

translations.literal: After He and Deng, the two Lis and three Yangs.
translations.idiomatic: After He and Deng came the two Lis and three Yangs.

sentences.zh: 偷權報怨，任國存亡。

translations.literal: Stealing power and repaying grudges, they entrusted the state's survival or destruction.
translations.idiomatic: They stole power to settle grudges and held the survival of the state in their hands.

sentences.zh: 書茲覆轍，敢告巖廊！

translations.literal: Recording this overturned track, I dare announce it to the cliff gallery!
translations.idiomatic: We inscribe this overturned chariot track as a warning to those in the halls of power!
